<!-- GENERATED by Tyhp.Domain.Diagnostics.DiagnosticsReferenceGenerator — do not edit message entries by hand. Regenerate from the compiler repo: scripts/sync-diagnostics-reference.sh -->

This page is the comprehensive index of Tyhp compiler diagnostic codes. Every entry is
generated from the compiler's code registry (`MessageCode.cs`) and the localized short-message
catalog (`.resx`), so the message text always matches what the compiler emits.

:::note
Diagnostic codes are stable identifiers. Once assigned, a code number always refers to the same
diagnostic, even across compiler versions. The canonical list of codes lives in
`Tyhp/Domain/Exceptions/MessageCode.cs`.
:::

:::tip
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP####</code> (or <code>tyhp explain ####</code>) to print the
long-form explanation for any code. That command reads the same dynamic catalog as this page.
:::

## Looking up a code

```bash
tyhp --explain TYHP4008
tyhp explain 4008
tyhp explain --code=TYHP3003
```

## Parser Errors (TYHP1xxx)

Parser errors occur during the ANTLR4 lexing and parsing phase when the compiler encounters syntax it cannot understand.

:::member[TYHP1001 (Error, Warning)]
**ParserUnknownError.** Message: <code>Unknown parser error: {0}</code>.

A catch-all for parser/lexer errors that do not match a more specific code. The `{0}` placeholder contains the underlying error message from the ANTLR4 parser.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
// Invalid token that confuses the lexer
class #invalid { }
```

Fix: Examine the indicated line and column for syntax errors. Ensure all tokens are valid Tyhp/PHP syntax.
:::

:::member[TYHP1002 (Error)]
**ParserUnexpectedError.** Message: <code>Unexpected token `{0}` at position {1}</code>.

The parser encountered a token it did not expect at the current position. This usually indicates a missing semicolon, unmatched brace, or misplaced keyword.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function greet(string $name) string {
    // Missing colon before return type ^^^
    return "Hello, $name";
}
```

Fix: Check the line for missing punctuation (semicolons, colons, braces, parentheses) or misplaced keywords. The correct syntax above is `function greet(string $name): string`.
:::

:::member[TYHP1003 (Error)]
**ParserCompileAborted.** Message: <code>Compilation aborted: {0}</code>.

The parser encountered too many errors and aborted processing for the current file. Earlier errors in the same file typically cause this.

Fix: Fix the earlier parser errors in the same file and recompile. Once the foundational syntax issues are resolved, this error will no longer appear.
:::

:::member[TYHP1004 (Error)]
**LexerCloseTagNotAllowedInTaglessMode.** Message: <code>Closing tag `?&gt;` is not allowed when `source.tagless` is enabled</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP1004</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::


## Visitor Errors (TYHP2xxx)

Visitor errors occur during parse-tree to AST conversion when the visitor encounters an unexpected structure or unsupported construct.

:::member[TYHP2001 (Error)]
**VisitorUnknownError.** Message: <code>Unknown visitor error</code>.

A catch-all for unexpected errors during AST generation. This typically indicates an internal compiler issue.

Fix: If you encounter this error, simplify the code near the indicated location and try again. If the error persists, please report it as a compiler bug.
:::

:::member[TYHP2002 (Error)]
**VisitorUnexpectedAlternative.** Message: <code>Unexpected grammar alternative `{1}` in rule `{0}`</code>.

The visitor hit an unexpected grammar alternative while walking the parse tree (a production the AST builder does not handle). This may occur with unusual or edge-case syntax combinations.

Fix: Simplify the expression or statement. If the syntax is valid PHP/Tyhp, this may indicate a compiler limitation -- please report it.
:::

:::member[TYHP2003 (Error)]
**VisitorMissingRequiredNode.** Message: <code>Required AST node missing in rule `{0}`</code>.

A required component of a language construct was not found in the parse tree. This often results from incomplete or malformed syntax.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
// Missing class body
class User
```

Fix: Ensure the construct is syntactically complete. Classes need bodies (`{ }`), functions need parameter lists and bodies, etc.
:::

:::member[TYHP2004 (Error)]
**VisitorUnsupportedConstruct.** Message: <code>Language construct `{0}` is not yet supported</code>.

The code uses a PHP language construct that the Tyhp compiler does not yet support.

Fix: Use an alternative approach that is supported by the compiler. Check the Tyhp documentation for supported constructs and any known limitations.
:::


## Binder Errors (TYHP3xxx)

Binder errors occur during symbol resolution and scope management.

:::member[TYHP3001 (Error, Warning)]
**BinderUnknownError.** Message: <code>Unknown binder error: {0}</code>.

A catch-all for unexpected errors during the binding phase.

Fix: If you encounter this error, please report it as a compiler bug with a minimal reproduction.
:::

:::member[TYHP3002 (Error)]
**BinderDuplicateSymbolDeclaration.** Message: <code>Duplicate declaration of symbol `{0}`</code>.

Two declarations with the same name exist in the same scope. This includes classes, functions, constants, and variables declared at the same scope level.

The primary span is the later declaration. A secondary span labeled "declared here" points at the first declaration of that name.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
class User { }  // first declaration — labeled "declared here"
class User { }  // Error: Duplicate declaration of symbol `User`
```

Fix: Rename one of the duplicate declarations, or remove the duplicate. If the declarations are in different files, ensure they are in different namespaces.
:::

:::member[TYHP3003 (Error)]
**BinderSymbolNotFound.** Message: <code>Symbol `{0}` is not found</code>.

A referenced class, function, constant, variable, or other symbol could not be resolved in any accessible scope. Type names on `is` / `instanceof` / `typeof`, and undeclared names inside generic type arguments, use this same diagnostic.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function demo(mixed $x): bool {
    return $x is UnknownType;  // Error: Symbol `UnknownType` is not found
}
```

Fix: Add a `use` statement to import the symbol, check for typos in the name, verify the symbol is defined in a loaded tyhpdef file, or ensure the file defining the symbol is included in the project.
:::

:::member[TYHP3004 (Error)]
**BinderInvalidSymbolTypeForParent.** Message: <code>Symbol type `{0}` is not valid for parent scope `{1}`</code>.

A symbol was declared in a scope where that type of declaration is not allowed.

Fix: Move the declaration to an appropriate scope. For example, class declarations belong at the namespace level, not inside function bodies.
:::

:::member[TYHP3005 (Error)]
**BinderInvalidFileScopeArgument.** Message: <code>Invalid argument for file scope</code>.

An internal error indicating an invalid configuration was passed to the file scope during binding.
:::

:::member[TYHP3006 (Error)]
**BinderCircularInheritance.** Message: <code>Circular inheritance detected involving `{0}`</code>.

A class or interface directly or indirectly extends or implements itself, creating an inheritance cycle.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
class A extends B { }
class B extends A { }  // Error: Circular inheritance
```

Fix: Break the inheritance cycle by removing or restructuring the class hierarchy.
:::

:::member[TYHP3007 (Error)]
**BinderTraitConflict.** Message: <code>Trait method conflict: `{0}`</code>.

Two or more traits used by the same class declare methods with the same name, and no conflict resolution (`insteadof` or `as`) was provided.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
trait A { public function hello(): void { } }
trait B { public function hello(): void { } }

class MyClass {
    use A, B;  // Error: Trait method conflict: 'hello'
}
```

Fix: Use `insteadof` to resolve the conflict: `use A, B { A::hello insteadof B; }`.
:::

:::member[TYHP3008 (Error)]
**BinderDuplicateUseAlias.** Message: <code>Duplicate use alias `{0}`</code>.

Two `use` import statements bring in symbols with the same alias name.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
use App\Models\User;
use App\DTOs\User;  // Error: Duplicate use alias 'User'
```

Fix: Use an alias to disambiguate: `use App\DTOs\User as UserDTO;`.
:::

:::member[TYHP3009 (Error)]
**BinderInvalidSelfReference.** Message: <code>Invalid `self` reference outside of a class</code>.

The keyword `self` was used outside of a class, interface, trait, or enum body.

Fix: Use `self` only within class-like declarations. Outside of a class, use the fully-qualified class name instead.
:::

:::member[TYHP3010 (Error)]
**BinderInvalidParentReference.** Message: <code>Invalid `parent` reference: class has no parent</code>.

The keyword `parent` was used in a class that does not extend another class.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
class Standalone {
    public function test(): void {
        parent::test();  // Error: class has no parent
    }
}
```

Fix: Add an `extends` clause to the class, or remove the `parent` reference.
:::

:::member[TYHP3011 (Error)]
**BinderDuplicateGenericParameter.** Message: <code>Duplicate generic type parameter `{0}`</code>.

A generic class or function declares two type parameters with the same name.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
class Container<T, T> { }  // Error: Duplicate generic type parameter 'T'
```

Fix: Give each generic type parameter a unique name.
:::

:::member[TYHP3012 (Error)]
**BinderGenericParameterShadow.** Message: <code>Generic type parameter `{0}` shadows an existing type</code>.

A generic type parameter has the same name as an existing class, interface, or type alias in scope.

Fix: Rename the generic type parameter to avoid shadowing (e.g., use `TItem` instead of `User`).
:::

:::member[TYHP3013 (Error)]
**BinderMultipleConstructors.** Message: <code>Class `{0}` declares multiple constructors</code>.

A class declares more than one `__construct` method. PHP and Tyhp only allow a single constructor per class.

Fix: Merge the constructors into a single `__construct` method with optional parameters, or use static factory methods for alternative construction patterns.
:::

:::member[TYHP3014 (Error)]
**ExtensionOperatorMissingTarget.** Message: <code>Operator overload in an extension is missing the required `&lt;Type&gt;` target</code>.

An `operator` declared inside an `extension` body must specify the type it extends using the `<Type>` target syntax.
:::

:::member[TYHP3015 (Error)]
**ExtensionOperatorTargetNotAllowed.** Message: <code>`&lt;Type&gt;` on an operator overload is only allowed inside an extension declaration</code>.

The `<Type>` target on an operator is only valid within an `extension` declaration, not on a class-member operator.
:::

:::member[TYHP3016 (Error)]
**ExtensionOperatorTargetNotFound.** Message: <code>The `&lt;Type&gt;` target of an extension operator does not resolve to a class or built-in type</code>.

The type named as the target of an extension operator overload does not resolve to a known class.
:::

:::member[TYHP3017 (Error)]
**BinderUnresolvedExtendsType.** Message: <code>Extends type `{0}` is not resolved</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP3017</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP3018 (Error)]
**BinderUnresolvedImplementsType.** Message: <code>Implements type `{0}` is not resolved</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP3018</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP3019 (Error)]
**BinderUnresolvedReturnType.** Message: <code>Return type `{0}` is not resolved</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP3019</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP3020 (Error)]
**BinderUnresolvedParameterType.** Message: <code>Parameter type `{0}` is not resolved</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP3020</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP3021 (Error)]
**BinderUnresolvedGenericConstraintType.** Message: <code>Generic constraint type `{0}` is not resolved</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP3021</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP3022 (Error)]
**BinderUnresolvedGenericDefaultType.** Message: <code>Generic default type `{0}` is not resolved</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP3022</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP3023 (Error)]
**BinderInvalidExtendsTypeKind.** Message: <code>Extends type `{0}` is a `{1}`, not a `{2}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP3023</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP3024 (Error)]
**BinderInvalidImplementsTypeKind.** Message: <code>Implements type `{0}` is a `{1}`, not an interface</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP3024</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP3025 (Error)]
**ExtensionOperatorTargetNotInstantiable.** Message: <code>The `&lt;Type&gt;` target of an extension operator cannot be `{0}`</code>.

The target of an extension operator must be a class or a value-bearing built-in type such as `string`, `int`, or `array`. Types that cannot be instantiated or used as a runtime value (`void`, `never`, `null`, `mixed`, `resource`, `true`, `false`) are not valid targets.
:::

:::member[TYHP3026 (Error)]
**BinderExternExtendsType.** Message: <code>Extends type `{0}` is extern</code>.

A type `extends` an `extern` placeholder. That name is bound, so this is not an unresolved `extends` (`TYHP3017`). Placeholders cannot be inheritance bases: a real tyhpdef class or interface must not extend an extern type.

The primary span is the `extends` clause. A secondary span labeled "declared here" points at the `extern` declaration. When that declaration has `// @provided-by: tyhpdef/ruflin-elastica` or `// @provided-by: tyhpdef/php-ext-curl`, help cites that wrapper name as-is.

Omit generated types that would extend an extern (for example a test base). Include the providing `tyhpdef/*` package if the intent is a real parent type.
:::

:::member[TYHP3027 (Error)]
**BinderExternImplementsType.** Message: <code>Implements type `{0}` is extern</code>.

A type `implements` an `extern` placeholder. That name is bound, so this is not an unresolved `implements` (`TYHP3018`). Placeholders cannot be interface lists: a real tyhpdef class or enum must not implement an extern type.

The primary span is the `implements` clause. A secondary span labeled "declared here" points at the `extern` declaration. When that declaration has `// @provided-by: tyhpdef/ruflin-elastica` or `// @provided-by: tyhpdef/php-ext-curl`, help cites that wrapper name as-is.

Omit generated types that would implement an extern. Include the providing `tyhpdef/*` package if the intent is a real interface.
:::

:::member[TYHP3028 (Error)]
**BinderTypeAliasConflictsWithFunction.** Message: <code>Type alias `{0}` conflicts with a function of the same name</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP3028</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP3029 (Error)]
**BinderCircularTypeAlias.** Message: <code>Circular type alias `{0}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP3029</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP3030 (Error)]
**BinderTypeAliasReservedFunctionName.** Message: <code>Type alias `{0}` cannot be a PHP function name</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP3030</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP3031 (Error)]
**BinderOverloadMissingImplementation.** Message: <code>Overload signature `{0}` has no implementation; overload signatures must be followed directly by a declaration with a body</code>.

Bodyless signatures of the same function or method name form an overload set only when a declaration with a body follows them directly (interface and `abstract` method sets are the exception: the signatures are the whole set). Add the implementation after the last signature.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function area(int $r): float;
function area(int $w, int $h): float;
// Error: no implementation follows. Add:
// function area(int $a, int $b = 0): float {
//     return $b === 0 ? 3.14159 * $a * $a : (float) ($a * $b);
// }
```
:::

:::member[TYHP3032 (Error)]
**BinderOverloadNotAdjacent.** Message: <code>Overload signature `{0}` must be declared directly before its implementation, with no other declarations in between</code>.

Keep the signatures and the implementation of one overload set together, in that order, with nothing declared between them.
:::

:::member[TYHP3033 (Warning)]
**BinderOverloadLone.** Message: <code>`{0}` has a single overload signature; declare at least two overloads, or remove it and use the implementation's own signature</code>.

A set with one signature hides the implementation's signature without adding a second call shape.
:::

:::member[TYHP3034 (Error)]
**BinderOverloadDuplicate.** Message: <code>Overload signature `{0}` has the same parameters and return type as an earlier overload</code>.

The first matching signature always wins, so an identical later signature can never be selected. Remove it or change its parameter types.
:::

:::member[TYHP3035 (Error)]
**BinderOverloadModifierMismatch.** Message: <code>Overload signature `{0}` must use the same modifiers (static, visibility, async, abstract, final) as the rest of its overload set</code>.

Every signature of a method overload set and its implementation share one set of modifiers.
:::

:::member[TYHP3036 (Error)]
**BinderOverloadConstructorNotSupported.** Message: <code>Overload signatures are not supported on constructors or destructors (`{0}`); declare separate factory methods or use optional parameters</code>.
:::


## Checker Errors (TYHP4xxx)

Checker errors occur during type checking and semantic analysis.

:::member[TYHP4001 (Error)]
**CheckerUnknownError.** Message: <code>Unknown checker error: {0}</code>.

A catch-all for unexpected errors during the checking phase.
:::

:::member[TYHP4002 (Error)]
**CheckerMultipleVisibilities.** Message: <code>`{0}` cannot have multiple visibility modifiers</code>.

A class member has multiple visibility keywords (`public`, `protected`, `private`).

```tyhp
<?tyhp
class Example {
    public protected string $name;  // Error: Multiple visibility modifiers
}
```

Fix: Use only one visibility modifier per declaration.
:::

:::member[TYHP4003 (Error)]
**CheckerNotAllowedMemberModifier.** Message: <code>Modifier `{0}` is not allowed here</code>.

A modifier is used in a context where it is not valid.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
interface Cacheable {
    static function getCacheKey(): string;
    // Error: 'static' is not allowed on interface methods
}
```

Fix: Remove the disallowed modifier. Check what modifiers are valid for the current context (interface, trait, enum, etc.).
:::

:::member[TYHP4004 (Error)]
**CheckerAccessorVisibilityCannotBeMoreVisibleThanProperty.** Message: <code>Accessor visibility cannot be more visible than property visibility; `{0}` is more visible than `{1}`</code>.

A property hook's (`get`/`set`) visibility is more permissive than the property itself.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
class Example {
    private string $name {
        public get => $this->name;  // Error: accessor more visible than property
    }
}
```

Fix: Make the accessor visibility equal to or more restrictive than the property visibility.
:::

:::member[TYHP4005 (Error)]
**CheckerMemberModifierConflict.** Message: <code>Member modifier `{0}` cannot be used at the same time as `{1}`</code>.

Two modifiers on the same declaration are mutually exclusive.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
class Example {
    abstract final function process(): void;
    // Error: Conflicting modifiers: 'abstract' and 'final'
}
```

Fix: Remove one of the conflicting modifiers. A method cannot be both `abstract` and `final`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4006 (Error)]
**CheckerInvalidPropertyAccessorType.** Message: <code>Invalid property accessor type `{0}`</code>.

The property hook type is not recognized (must be `get` or `set`).
:::

:::member[TYHP4007 (Error)]
**CheckerParameterNotAllowedOnPropertyAccessorType.** Message: <code>Parameter declaration is not allowed on property accessor of type `{0}`</code>.

A `get` accessor declares a parameter, which is not valid. Only `set` accessors accept a value parameter.
:::

:::member[TYHP4008 (Error)]
**CheckerTypeMismatch.** Message: <code>Cannot assign type `{0}` to type `{1}`</code>.

The checker reports a type mismatch when a value's type is not assignable to the type its target declares — an assignment, an argument, a return statement, or a property initializer. The first placeholder is the type of the value being supplied; the second is the type the target requires.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
int $count = "hello";
// Error: Cannot assign type 'string' to type 'int'
```

Make the two types agree: widen or change the declared type, convert the value explicitly, or narrow a nullable or union type with a guard before the assignment.

A generic class written without type arguments is `Box<mixed>` when it is assigned to an instantiation of the same class, so `Box<int> $b = $raw;` with a `Box $raw` reports this error, as do the same assignment through an argument (TYHP4010) or a return (TYHP4009). The reverse direction is fine. See [Generic Types Without Type Arguments](tyhp_0500_generics.md#generic-types-without-type-arguments).
:::

:::member[TYHP4009 (Error)]
**CheckerIncompatibleReturnType.** Message: <code>Return type `{0}` is not compatible with declared return type `{1}`</code>.

A function or method returns a value whose type does not match its declared return type.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function getName(): string {
    return 42;  // Error: Return type 'int' is not compatible with 'string'
}
```

Fix: Change the return value to match the declared return type, or update the return type declaration.
:::

:::member[TYHP4010 (Error)]
**CheckerIncompatibleArgumentType.** Message: <code>Argument of type `{0}` is not assignable to parameter of type `{1}`</code>.

A function or method call passes an argument whose type does not match the expected parameter type.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function process(int $id): void { }
process("abc");  // Error: Argument of type 'string' not assignable to 'int'
```

Fix: Pass a value of the correct type, or cast the argument explicitly.

An implicit [`operator convert`](tyhp_1600_operatorOverloads.md) lets a call pass a convertible argument, but a conversion declared in an extension applies only where the extension is active (the declaring file, a file with `use extension`, or any file once `global use extension` is declared). Elsewhere the same call reports this error. A variable declared `callable(Money): string` and a closure also keep their exact parameter types, so passing a convertible argument to either reports this error.
:::

:::member[TYHP4011 (Error)]
**CheckerMissingReturnStatement.** Message: <code>Function with return type `{0}` must return a value on all code paths</code>.

A non-void function has code paths that do not return a value.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function getStatus(bool $active): string {
    if ($active) {
        return "active";
    }
    // Error: not all code paths return a value
}
```

Fix: Add a return statement for every code path, including `else` branches and after loops.
:::

:::member[TYHP4012 (Warning)]
**CheckerUnreachableCode.** Message: <code>Unreachable code detected</code>.

Code exists after a `return`, `throw`, `break`, `continue`, or `exit` statement and will never execute.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function example(): string {
    return "done";
    echo "this never runs";  // Warning: Unreachable code
}
```

Fix: Remove the unreachable code or restructure the control flow.
:::

:::member[TYHP4013 (Error)]
**CheckerVariableUsedBeforeAssignment.** Message: <code>Variable `${0}` is used before being assigned</code>.

A variable is read before it has been assigned a value on any code path.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function example(): void {
    echo $x;  // Error: Variable '$x' is used before being assigned
    int $x = 5;
}
```

Fix: Assign the variable before using it.
:::

:::member[TYHP4014 (Error)]
**CheckerVariablePossiblyUndefined.** Message: <code>Variable `${0}` is possibly undefined</code>.

A variable may not be defined on all code paths leading to its use.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function example(bool $flag): void {
    if ($flag) {
        string $msg = "yes";
    }
    echo $msg;  // Error: '$msg' is possibly undefined
}
```

Fix: Initialize the variable before the conditional, or add an `else` branch that also assigns it.
:::

:::member[TYHP4015 (Error)]
**CheckerVariablePossiblyNull.** Message: <code>Variable `${0}` is possibly null here but is used where a non-null value is required</code>.

A variable with a nullable type is used in a context that requires a non-null value without a prior null check.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function example(?string $name): void {
    echo \strlen($name);  // Warning: '$name' is possibly null
}
```

Fix: Add a null check before using the variable, or use the null coalescing operator `??`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4016 (Error)]
**CheckerVariableTypeRequired.** Message: <code>`{0}` must have a type annotation or inferable initializer</code>.

A variable, parameter, or property lacks both an explicit type declaration and an initializer from which the type can be inferred. A function or method with no return type uses the same diagnostic with the subject `return type`.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function example($x) {
    return $x;
}
```

Fix: Annotate the parameter and return type (`function example(int $x): int`). For a local variable, add an explicit type (`int $x;`) or an initializer (`$x = 0;`).
:::

:::member[TYHP4017 (Error)]
**CheckerAbstractMethodNotImplemented.** Message: <code>Class `{0}` does not implement abstract method `{1}` from `{2}`</code>.

A concrete class extends an abstract class but does not implement all of its abstract methods.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
abstract class Shape {
    abstract public function area(): float;
}

class Circle extends Shape {
    // Error: does not implement abstract method 'area' from 'Shape'
}
```

Fix: Implement all abstract methods from the parent class with matching signatures.
:::

:::member[TYHP4018 (Error)]
**CheckerInterfaceMethodNotImplemented.** Message: <code>Class `{0}` does not implement interface method `{1}` from `{2}`</code>.

A class implements an interface but does not provide implementations for all of its methods.
:::

:::member[TYHP4019 (Error)]
**CheckerFinalClassExtended.** Message: <code>Cannot extend final class `{0}`</code>.

A class attempts to extend a class that is declared as `final`.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
final class Singleton { }
class MySingleton extends Singleton { }  // Error: Cannot extend final class
```
:::

:::member[TYHP4020 (Error)]
**CheckerFinalMethodOverridden.** Message: <code>Cannot override final method `{0}`</code>.

A subclass attempts to override a method that is declared as `final` in the parent class.
:::

:::member[TYHP4021 (Error)]
**CheckerReadonlyPropertyReassigned.** Message: <code>Cannot assign to readonly property `{0}`</code>.

A `readonly` property is being assigned outside of the constructor.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
class User {
    public function __construct(
        public readonly string $name
    ) {}

    public function rename(string $newName): void {
        $this->name = $newName;  // Error: Cannot assign to readonly property
    }
}
```
:::

:::member[TYHP4022 (Error)]
**CheckerAbstractClassInstantiated.** Message: <code>Cannot instantiate abstract class `{0}`</code>.

Code attempts to create an instance of an abstract class with `new`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4023 (Error)]
**CheckerEnumCaseTypeMismatch.** Message: <code>Enum case value type `{0}` does not match backed type `{1}`</code>.

A backed enum case has a value of a type that does not match the enum's backing type.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
enum Status: string {
    case Active = 1;  // Error: int value for string-backed enum
}
```
:::

:::member[TYHP4024 (Error)]
**CheckerEnumMethodNotAllowed.** Message: <code>Enum cannot have a constructor</code>.

An enum declares a method that is not allowed (e.g., a constructor).
:::

:::member[TYHP4025 (Error)]
**CheckerMemberNotAccessible.** Message: <code>`{0}` is `{1}` and cannot be accessed from `{2}`</code>.

A private or protected member is accessed from outside its allowed scope.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
class Account {
    private float $balance = 0.0;
}

Account $a = new Account();
$a->balance;  // Error: Cannot access private member 'balance'
```
:::

:::member[TYHP4026 (Error)]
**CheckerBreakOutsideLoop.** Message: <code>`break` statement is not within a loop or switch</code>.

A `break` statement appears outside of a `for`, `foreach`, `while`, `do-while`, or `switch` block.
:::

:::member[TYHP4027 (Error)]
**CheckerContinueOutsideLoop.** Message: <code>`continue` statement is not within a loop</code>.

A `continue` statement appears outside of a loop construct.
:::

:::member[TYHP4028 (Error)]
**CheckerAwaitOutsideAsync.** Message: <code>`await` can only be used inside an async function</code>.

The `await` keyword, or `using await`, is used inside a function that is not marked as `async`.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function fetchData(): string {
    return await getRemoteData();  // Error: await outside of async function
}

function closeAll(): void {
    using await ($conn = new AsyncConnection()) { }  // Error: using await outside async code
}
```

Fix: Mark the function as `async`: `async function fetchData(): Promise<string>`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4029 (Error)]
**CheckerInvalidOperatorForType.** Message: <code>Operator `{0}` cannot be applied to types `{1}` and `{2}`</code>.

A binary or unary operator is used with operands whose types do not support that operation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4030 (Error)]
**CheckerDisposableRequiresInterface.** Message: <code>Resource of `:=`, `using` or `using await` requires a type implementing `IsDisposable`</code>.

The disposable assignment operator `:=`, a `using` block, or a `using await` block is used with a class that implements neither `IsDisposable` nor `AsyncIsDisposable`.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
class PlainObject { }
$obj := new PlainObject();
// Error: ':=' requires the type to implement IsDisposable

using (PlainObject $p = new PlainObject()) { }
// Error: same requirement
```
:::

:::member[TYHP4031 (Error)]

The `with` keyword references a property name that does not exist on the target type.

:::member[TYHP4032 (Error)]

A function with a type guard return type (`$param is Type`) does not return a boolean value.

:::member[TYHP4035 (Error)]
**CheckerGenericConstraintNotSatisfied.** Message: <code>Type `{0}` does not satisfy constraint `{1}`</code>.

A type argument provided for a generic parameter does not meet the declared constraint. A `mixed` argument binds the parameter to `mixed`, so it fails any constraint other than `mixed`; narrow the value first.

```tyhp
<?tyhp

// Error: 'string' does not satisfy constraint 'Entity'
Repository<string> $repo = new Repository<string>();
```
:::

A type argument passed to a utility type does not meet that utility's constraints (for example, requiring an object type).

:::member[TYHP4052 (Warning)]
**CheckerReferenceTypeChanged.** Message: <code>Reference parameter `{0}` reassigned to type `{1}`, which differs from declared type `{2}`</code>.

A by-reference parameter was reassigned to a value whose type differs from the parameter's declared type. Callers sharing that reference may observe an unexpected type.

:::member[TYHP4053 (Error)]
**CheckerDuplicateTypeInComposite.** Message: <code>Type `{0}` appears more than once in a union or intersection type</code>.

The same type appears more than once in a union or intersection (for example `int|int` or `A&A`).

Fix: Remove the duplicate member from the composite type.
:::

:::member[TYHP4054 (Error)]
**CheckerMixedInComposite.** Message: <code>`mixed` or `never` cannot be used in union or intersection types</code>.

`mixed` and `never` cannot appear as members of a union or intersection because they absorb or contradict the other members.

Fix: Remove `mixed`/`never` from the composite, or replace the composite with `mixed` / `never` alone when that is the intended type.
:::

:::member[TYHP4055 (Error)]
**CheckerRedundantTypeInUnion.** Message: <code>Redundant type `{0}` in union type</code>.

A union member is redundant because a wider member of the same union already covers it, so removing it does not change the set of values. Typical cases are `bool|false`, `object|User`, and `iterable|array`.

This is different from a duplicated member (`int|int`), which is TYHP4053.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
bool|false $flag;
object|User $entity;
```

Fix: Remove the redundant member from the union.
:::

:::member[TYHP4056 (Error)]
**CheckerUseBoolInsteadOfTrueFalse.** Message: <code>Use `bool` instead of `true|false`</code>.

The union `true|false` is exactly the `bool` type. Spell it as `bool` instead of listing both boolean literals.

Fix: Replace `true|false` with `bool`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4057 (Error)]
**CheckerNonClassInIntersection.** Message: <code>Non-class type `{0}` cannot appear in intersection types</code>.

Intersection types (`A&B`) may only contain class-like members (classes, interfaces, and similar). A non-class type such as a scalar or `array` cannot appear in an intersection.

Fix: Use a union (`|`) when mixing scalars with objects, or drop the non-class member.
:::

:::member[TYHP4058 (Error)]
**CheckerCallableNotAllowedOnProperty.** Message: <code>`callable` cannot be used as a property type declaration</code>.

A property (including a promoted constructor parameter) cannot be declared with the `callable` type. PHP does not allow `callable` on properties.

Fix: Use `\Closure`, an interface, or a named class type instead of `callable`.

:::member[TYHP4059 (Error)]
**CheckerVoidNotAllowedHere.** Message: <code>`void` can only be used as a return type</code>.

`void` is only valid as a function or method return type. It cannot be used as a parameter type or property type (see also TYHP4048 for `void` as a generic type argument).

Fix: Use a different type, or `mixed` when "no value" is intended.

:::member[TYHP4060 (Warning)]
**CheckerVoidRefReturn.** Message: <code>Returning by reference from a `void` function is deprecated</code>.

A function or method declared `void` uses a by-reference return (`function &foo(): void`). Returning by reference from a `void` function is deprecated in PHP.

Fix: Drop the `&` or give the function a non-void return type.

:::member[TYHP4061 (Error)]
**CheckerNeverNotAllowedHere.** Message: <code>`never` can only be used as a return type</code>.

`never` is rejected as a parameter type or a property type. It is a valid generic type argument and a valid return type.

Fix: Use a different type for parameters and properties.
:::

:::member[TYHP4062 (Error)]
**CheckerResourceNotAllowed.** Message: <code>`resource` cannot be used in user type declarations</code>.

`resource` is a historical PHP runtime type and cannot be written in user type declarations. Tyhp does not accept `resource` as a parameter, return, property, or alias type.

Fix: Use a class or interface that wraps the resource, or `mixed` if the value is intentionally untyped.

:::member[TYHP4063 (Error)]
**CheckerRefArgMustBeVariable.** Message: <code>By-reference argument must be a variable, not a literal or expression</code>.

A by-reference parameter must be passed a variable (or a dereferenceable location such as an array element or object property). Literals and temporary expressions cannot be passed by reference.

Fix: Store the value in a variable and pass that variable.

:::member[TYHP4064 (Error)]
**CheckerRelativeTypeOutsideClass.** Message: <code>`self` or `parent` used outside class context</code>.

`self` and `parent` name the enclosing class or its parent. They are not valid outside a class, interface, trait, or enum body (for example in a file-level function).

Fix: Use a named type, or move the declaration into a class-like body.

:::member[TYHP4065 (Error)]
**CheckerParentWithoutParent.** Message: <code>`parent` used in class `{0}` that has no parent class</code>.

Fix: Add an `extends` clause, or replace `parent` with a named type or `self`.

:::member[TYHP4066 (Error)]
**CheckerStaticNotReturnType.** Message: <code>`static` cannot be used as a parameter or property type</code>.

`static` is a late-binding return type (and is allowed in locals, `instanceof`, and generic arguments). It cannot be used as a parameter type or a property type.

Fix: Use `self`, a named class, or a generic parameter instead of `static` on parameters and properties.

:::member[TYHP4067 (Error)]

:::member[TYHP4101 (Error)]
**CheckerSymbolNameNotFound.** Message: <code>Symbol `{0}` is not found for type `{1}`</code>.

A property read, method call, or static member access whose receiver type has no such member. This covers instance members of a fully-known class or interface (including bare `object`, which has no members) as well as scalar and other built-in receivers. The error is not reported when the class has a magic accessor (`__get`, `__call`, `__callStatic`), when part of its ancestry is unresolved, or when the member name is dynamic (`$obj->{$name}`).

Inside the branch of `\property_exists($obj, 'name')` or `\method_exists($obj, 'name')` with a literal name, that member is known to exist.

For a scalar or other built-in receiver, or a class, this is also what you see when the method belongs to an extension that is not in scope in the current file. A project-source extension applies in the file that declares it, in files that import it with `use extension`, and everywhere when a file declares it with `global use extension`.

```tyhp
<?tyhp

// In a file that neither declares nor imports an extension with `shout()` on string:
string $s = 'c';
echo $s->shout();   // Error: Symbol `shout` is not found for type `string`
```

Fix: Add `use extension \Your\Extension;` to the file, or call a method the type has.
:::

:::member[TYHP4118 (Error)]

```tyhp

function narrow(int $a): int;
function narrow(string $a): string;
function narrow(int $a): int {   // the implementation does not accept `string`
    return $a;
}
```
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4118</code> for the long-form explanation.

:::member[TYHP4121 (Warning)]
**CheckerEmptyCatch.** Message: <code>Empty `catch` block silently swallows exceptions</code>.

An empty `catch` block has no statements, so the exception is swallowed with no handling. That is often accidental.

When swallowing is intentional, name the exception and discard it with `(void)` — the same discard used for unused `#[\NoDiscard]` returns. `(void)$e` is a statement, so the catch body is not empty, and it records that the value is unused on purpose. A comment-only body is still empty.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
try {
    $rp = new \ReflectionProperty($class, $name);
} catch (\ReflectionException $e) {
    (void)$e;
}
```
:::

:::member[TYHP4127 (Error)]
**CheckerAttributeTargetMismatch.** Message: <code>Attribute `{0}` cannot be applied to {1}</code>.

The attribute is not valid on this kind of declaration. PHP Core attributes declare allowed targets (`TARGET_METHOD`, `TARGET_PROPERTY`, and so on); applying one elsewhere is a target mismatch.

`#[\Override]` on a property is a target mismatch when `output.phpVersion` is below 8.5 (properties become a legal target at 8.5). On 8.5 or later, a property that does not actually override uses TYHP4129 instead.

When `output.phpVersion` is 8.5 or later, `#[\DelayedTargetValidation]` on the same declaration skips this target check for PHP Core attributes on that declaration. Functional checks still run: `#[\Override]` that does not override is still TYHP4129, unused `#[\NoDiscard]` returns are still TYHP4165, and `#[\Override]` on `__construct` is still TYHP4339. On `output.phpVersion` below 8.5, `#[\Override]` on a property is a target mismatch (TYHP4127), not this code. `#[\Override]` on `__construct` is always TYHP4339, even when a parent constructor exists.

Trait method bodies are not checked here; PHP applies the attribute on the composing class.

:::member[TYHP4157 (Error)]
**CheckerPropertyPossiblyUninitialized.** Message: <code>Typed property `${0}` is possibly uninitialized here; declare `?T ${0} = null`, add an initializer, or guard the read with `??` / `isset`</code>.

PHP throws "Typed property must not be accessed before initialization" when a typed property has no initializer, is not set by constructor property promotion, and has not been definitely assigned on every constructor path before it is read.

Prefer declaring the property as nullable with an explicit null default (`?T $prop = null`) when the code does not need to distinguish "no value" from "value is null". Otherwise assign it in the constructor on all paths, or guard the read with `??` / `isset` (which do not throw on uninitialized typed properties).

Assignment via a helper method called from the constructor does not count — only a direct `$this->prop = …` in the constructor body (or a declaration-level initializer / promoted parameter) is a guaranteed source.
:::

:::member[TYHP4158 (Error)]
**CheckerUnsetTypedPropertyWithoutAllowUnset.** Message: <code>Cannot `unset` typed property `${0}` without `#[\Tyhp\AllowUnset]`; prefer `?T ${0} = null`, or add the attribute when distinguishing uninitialized from null is required</code>.

PHP's unset() on a typed property returns the slot to the uninitialized state, which defeats property-initialization analysis.

Prefer declaring the property as nullable with an explicit null default (`?T $prop = null`) when "no value" and null are the same. Only opt in with `#[\Tyhp\AllowUnset]` when code genuinely needs the uninitialized state; then every unguarded read may report TYHP4157, and unset itself clears definite-initialization within the method.
:::

:::member[TYHP4159 (Error)]
**CheckerStructRequiredPropertyNotSet.** Message: <code>Required struct property `{0}` on `{1}` must be set via `new ... with [...]`</code>.

Struct properties that are non-nullable and have no default value are required. They cannot be omitted from construction — supply them with `new StructName() with [prop => value, ...]`.

Nullable properties (and properties with defaults) remain optional at construction.
:::

:::member[TYHP4160 (Error)]
**CheckerMixedRequiresNarrowing.** Message: <code>Type `mixed` must be narrowed before this use</code>.

`mixed` is Tyhp's strict top type: any value may be assigned to it, but it cannot be used in type-specific operations until narrowed.

Narrow with a type guard (`instanceof` / `is`, `\is_string()`, `\is_int()`, a user-defined `$param is T` guard, or a null check) before member access (including the receiver of `$m->p ?? 1` and `$m->p ??= 1`), calls, indexing, `$m::class`, array spread (`[...$m]`), arithmetic, bitwise ops, string concatenation, ordering comparisons (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `<=>`), or similar. Equality (`==`, `===`, `!=`, `!==`), `??`, casts, and `instanceof`/`is` themselves are allowed so narrowing remains possible.

Guards can be combined: after `\is_int($m) || $m === null`, `$m` is `?int`.

Assignment and return already reject passing `mixed` where a more specific type is required (TYHP4008 / TYHP4009 / TYHP4010).
:::

:::member[TYHP4161 (Error)]
**CheckerReservedPropertyHookMethodSuffix.** Message: <code>`{0}` ends with `{1}`, which is reserved for property-hook polyfill methods the compiler emits</code>.

PHP < 8.4 property-hook lowering emits private methods named `__get_<prop>__tyhpPropertyHook` and `__set_<prop>__tyhpPropertyHook`, then passes them as first-class callables into `PropertyAccessor` registration.

A user declaration ending with `__tyhpPropertyHook` would collide with those generated symbols. Rename the declaration.
:::

:::member[TYHP4162 (Error)]
**CheckerPipeRhsNotCallable.** Message: <code>Right-hand side of `|&gt;` is not callable</code>.

The pipe operator (`|>`) passes the left-hand value as the sole argument to the right-hand callable. The RHS must be a Closure, first-class callable, `callable`/`\Closure`-typed value, or an object with `__invoke`.

Replace the RHS with a single-argument callable (for example `strlen(...)` or `(fn($x) => …)`).
:::

:::member[TYHP4163 (Error)]
**CheckerPipeRhsInvalidArity.** Message: <code>Right-hand side of `|&gt;` must accept exactly one argument</code>.

The pipe operator (`|>`) has invalid arity: PHP pipes the left-hand value as a single argument. Callables with more than one required parameter, or with zero parameters, cannot be used on the RHS.

Wrap multi-argument callees in a Closure or arrow function that supplies the extra arguments, e.g. `(fn($x) => \str_replace('a', 'b', $x))`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4164 (Error)]
**CheckerPipeRhsByRefParameter.** Message: <code>Right-hand side of `|&gt;` must not take parameter `${0}` by reference</code>.

Piped values are temporaries, so callables whose first parameter is by-reference are rejected (for example `\array_pop(...)`).

Wrap the call in a Closure that takes the value by value and forwards a local variable by reference if mutation is required.
:::

:::member[TYHP4165 (Warning)]
**CheckerNoDiscardReturnUnused.** Message: <code>Return value of `{0}` is marked `#[\NoDiscard]` and must be used or discarded with `(void)`{1}</code>.

`#[\NoDiscard]` marks a function or method whose return value should be used. An unused return is TYHP4165. When `$message` is a string literal, that text is appended to the warning after a colon.

Use the return value (assignment, argument, condition, and so on), or cast with `(void)` to mark an intentional discard: `(void)important();`. Assignment to `$_` also counts as a use.

The warning comes from the invoked declaration. Calling through an interface or abstract method does not warn, even if that declaration is marked. An override does not inherit the warning unless it is itself marked. A trait-imported method keeps the attribute.

Tyhp reports this even when `output.phpVersion` is below 8.5 (PHP's runtime warning is a no-op on older minors). The `(void)` cast is native on 8.5 or later and is omitted from emitted PHP below 8.5.
:::

:::member[TYHP4166 (Error)]
**CheckerFinalPropertyHookOverridden.** Message: <code>Cannot override final property hook `{0}::${1}::{2}()`</code>.

PHP 8.4 rejects overriding a `final` property hook at class-declaration time, the same as overriding a final method. `final get` and `final set` are independent — only the hook marked `final` is sealed.

Remove the overriding hook from the child, or drop `final` from the ancestor hook if the override is intentional.
:::

:::member[TYHP4167 (Error)]
**CheckerByRefPropertyGetHookRequiresPhp84.** Message: <code>By-ref property hook `&amp;get` requires PHP `8.4` or later; target is `{0}`</code>.

PHP 8.4 native property hooks support `&get` so `$ref = &$obj->prop` (and array-element writes that rely on by-ref get) can alias backing storage.

When `output.phpVersion` is below 8.4, Tyhp lowers hooks through magic `__get`, which cannot return by reference. Emitting an ordinary by-value get would silently change program semantics, so Tyhp reports an error instead.

Raise `output.phpVersion` to `8.4` or later to keep native `&get`, or rewrite the property to a by-value `get` hook if by-ref aliasing is not required.
:::

:::member[TYHP4168 (Error)]
**CheckerParameterizedStaticForbidden.** Message: <code>Parameterized `static&lt;...&gt;` is not allowed; use bare `static`, `self&lt;...&gt;`, `parent&lt;...&gt;`, or an explicit class name</code>.

Tyhp forbids parameterized `static<...>` in every scope, including `final` classes.

Late-static binding names the late-bound class; it does not invent or rebind generic type arguments. Type arguments come from the call-site class spelling (`Child<string>::factory()`) or from the receiver/`$this` instantiation for instance methods.

Use: - bare `static` for fluent / LSB returns that should follow the late-bound class - `self<...>` or the declaring class name for factories that stamp method generics onto the class (e.g. `_async<T>(...): self<__Awaited<T>>`) - `parent<...>` when an explicit parent instantiation is required

```tyhp
final class Promise<TReturn extends __Awaited<void|mixed> = __Awaited<mixed>> {
    public static function _async<T extends void|mixed>(callable(): T $fn): self<__Awaited<T>> { /* ... */ }
    public function then<TResult>(callable(TReturn): TResult $cb): static { /* ... */ }
}
```
:::

Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4169</code> for the long-form explanation.

:::member[TYHP4171 (Error)]

Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4171</code> for the long-form explanation.

:::member[TYHP4172 (Error)]
**CheckerEmptyExtension.** Message: <code>Extension `{0}` must declare at least one member</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4172</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4173 (Error)]
**CheckerExtensionHideUnknownMember.** Message: <code>Extension member `{0}` does not exist and cannot be hidden</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4173</code> for the long-form explanation.
