:::member[TYHP4174 (Error)]
**CheckerInlineParameterMutation.** Message: <code>Spliced member `{0}` writes a parameter that is not declared `&amp;`, declares `&amp;` on a parameter it does not write, or mutates `$this` without `&amp;`</code>.

A spliced extension member substitutes the caller's argument where the parameter stood. A parameter the expression writes (assignment, compound assignment, `++` / `--` in either position, or passing to a callee's `&` parameter) must be declared `&`, and only those parameters may be. Write a non-mutating increment as `$v + 1`. Writing `$this` without the `&$this` receiver annotation is `TYHP4369`; annotating `&$this` on a member that never writes `$this` is `TYHP4370`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4175 (Error)]
**CheckerInlineCycle.** Message: <code>Spliced member `{0}` refers to itself, directly or through other spliced members</code>.

Reducing a spliced call must terminate. A member whose expression (after substituting other spliced members) refers back to itself would loop. Break the cycle or move the logic into a multi-statement member that Tyhp calls rather than splices.
:::

:::member[TYHP4176 (Error)]
**CheckerInlineAttributeOnExtensionMember.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\Optimize\Inline]` is not allowed on an extension member</code>.

Extension splicing is decided by the member's form (`=>` vs brace body), not by `#[\Tyhp\Optimize\Inline]`. Remove the attribute. On a Tyhp `extension { }` member, pick the form that matches whether PHP should keep a method.
:::

:::member[TYHP4177 (Error)]
**CheckerReservedInlineTempPrefix.** Message: <code>Variable `${0}` collides with the reserved inline temporary prefix `{1}`</code>.

The compiler introduces locals named `$__tyhpInlineTemp1`, `$__tyhpInlineTemp2`, … when a spliced parameter is used more than once. Do not declare a variable whose name starts with that prefix.
:::

:::member[TYHP4179 (Error)]
**CheckerInlineInaccessibleMember.** Message: <code>Spliced member `{0}` references `{1}`, which is less accessible than the member</code>.

A spliced expression is evaluated at the call site, not inside the declaring class. The body may only reference members at least as accessible as the spliced member itself: a public member's body may reference public members only; a protected body may reference protected and public; a private body may reference any member of the declaring class.
:::

:::member[TYHP4180 (Error)]
**CheckerNonReferenceableByRefArgument.** Message: <code>Argument for by-reference parameter `${0}` is not referenceable</code>.

A `&` parameter requires an argument PHP can bind as a reference. The receiver of a member annotated `&$this` is that argument. Literals, constants, call results, `readonly` properties, and properties whose read path is by value (`{ get; }` in tyhpdef, `__get`, or `offsetGet`) are not referenceable. A tyhpdef `{ &get; }` is. Pass a variable, a non-readonly stored property, or a `{ &get; }` / `&__get` / `&offsetGet` path instead.
:::

:::member[TYHP4181 (Error)]
**CheckerErasedMemberUnsafeSplice.** Message: <code>Call to erased member `{0}` cannot be spliced faithfully</code>.

A short `=>` Tyhp extension member and a tyhpdef thin mapping have no PHP method. If the call site cannot be spliced without dropping an argument, delaying it, reordering side effects, or needing a reference-bound local with no statement slot, the compiler reports this error. Bind the argument to a variable first, or (on a Tyhp `extension { }` member) switch to a single-`return` brace body so a PHP method exists to call.
:::

:::member[TYHP4182 (Error)]
**CheckerUndefinedFunction.** Message: <code>Function `{0}` is not found</code>.

A function call whose name does not resolve to any declared function, tyhpdef stub, `use function` import, or compile-time builtin is undefined. The binder does not bind call-site function names; the checker resolves them from the enclosing namespace, imports, and the global table. A PHP-version gate (`declare(php=…)` / `#[\Tyhp\Php]`) that is inactive for `output.phpVersion` omits the symbol, so a call outside that gate is the same error. Declare the function, import it, raise the compile target, or fix the name.
:::

:::member[TYHP4183 (Error)]
**CheckerCallableEllipsisNotAllowed.** Message: <code>`...` is not a type argument; write `callable(...): TReturn` for unknown arity</code>.

Bare `...` in a type-argument list is not a rest pack and not a trailing `T...`. Unknown-arity callables are written `callable(...): bool` as a generic bound (`T extends callable(...): bool`). `...` is not valid on `array`, `\Closure`, or user generics, and is not a call-site type argument (`identity<...>(1)`).
:::

:::member[TYHP4184 (Error)]
**CheckerCallableAnyArityNotAValueType.** Message: <code>`callable(...): {0}` cannot be used as a parameter, property, or return type; write `T extends callable(...): {0}` and use `T`</code>.

`callable(...): TReturn` pins a callback return type without pinning arity. The parameter list is unknown, so the facet is not a value type and is not invokable. Constrain a type parameter (`TCallable extends callable(...): bool`) and take `TCallable $callback` so inference can recover a concrete callable.
:::

:::member[TYHP4185 (Error)]
**CheckerCallableAnyArityNotInvokable.** Message: <code>Cannot call a value of type `{0}`; any-arity `callable(...): TReturn` is not invokable</code>.

A value typed as `callable(...): TReturn` has an unknown parameter list, so a call cannot be checked. Pass the value, store it, or recover a concrete callable via `TCallable extends callable(...): TReturn` and inference. Direct `callable(...): TReturn $cb` parameters are also rejected (TYHP4184).
:::

:::member[TYHP4186 (Error)]
**CheckerTypeAliasFactoryTypeArguments.** Message: <code>Type alias factory `{0}` cannot be called with type arguments; write `typeof({0}&lt;…&gt;)` or `{0}(typeof(…))`</code>.

A type alias factory is a PHP function over `\Tyhp\Type` values, not a generic function. `Optional<int>()` mixes type-argument syntax into a value call. Write `typeof(Optional<int>)` to get a Type value from a type, or `Optional(typeof(int))` / `Optional()` to call the factory with `\Tyhp\Type` arguments.
:::

:::member[TYHP4187 (Error)]
**CheckerCallablePackEllipsisNotAllowed.** Message: <code>A parameter pack cannot take postfix `...` as a type argument; write `callable(__CallableParametersRest&lt;T&gt; ...): R`</code>.

`__CallableParametersRest<T>` is a pack. On a callable shape it is an ordinary parameter (`callable(Rest<T> ...$args): R`) that splices T's parameters. Postfix `T...` as a generic type argument is not a splice marker.
:::

:::member[TYHP4188 (Error)]
**CheckerCallablePostfixEllipsisNotAllowed.** Message: <code>Postfix `T...` is not a type argument; write `callable(T ...$args): R` for a homogeneous variadic</code>.

`callable(T ...$args): R` spells a trailing PHP variadic on a callable shape. Postfix `T...` is not valid as a generic type argument on `array`, `\Closure`, or user generics. `int... $x` (ellipsis glued to the type) is not the PHP variadic `int ...$x`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4189 (Error)]
**CheckerCallableSliceOverlap.** Message: <code>`__CallableParametersSlice` uses of `{0}` overlap at parameter index {1}</code>.

Slices of one `TCallable` on the same function must be disjoint. A non-variadic `Slice<T, N> $x` occupies index N; a variadic `Slice<T, N> ...$xs` occupies N and every later index. Two slices that cover the same index overlap. Split the range or drop the duplicate slice.
:::

:::member[TYHP4190 (Error)]
**CheckerCallableSliceHole.** Message: <code>`__CallableParametersSlice` uses of `{0}` leave a hole at parameter index {1}</code>.

Slices of one `TCallable` must cover required parameters without holes, ordered by `TStart`. `Slice<T, 0> $x` followed by `Slice<T, 2> ...$rest` skips index 1. Add a slice for the missing index or start the rest slice at the next index.
:::

:::member[TYHP4191 (Error)]
**CheckerCallableSliceMinOnFixed.** Message: <code>`TMin` is only valid on a variadic `__CallableParametersSlice` parameter</code>.

A non-variadic `Slice<T, N> $x` is exactly parameter N. `TMin` counts how many arguments a variadic slice must receive (`Slice<T, 1, 1> ...$arrays`). Do not write the third type argument on a fixed Slice.
:::

:::member[TYHP4192 (Error)]
**CheckerCallableSliceIndexNotIntLiteral.** Message: <code>`__CallableParametersSlice` index `{0}` must be a non-negative int literal</code>.

`TStart` and `TMin` are non-negative integer literal types (`0`, `1`, …), the same family as `__IndexValueType<T, 0>`. A general `int`, a negative literal, or a type parameter is not an index.
:::

:::member[TYHP4193 (Error)]
**CheckerFileLevelTypedConstNotAllowed.** Message: <code>File-level `const` declarations cannot have a type annotation</code>.

PHP typed constants exist only on classes, interfaces, traits, and enums. Write `const X = 1;` at file scope, or move the constant onto a type. Tyhpdef file-level `const int X;` remains legal because those declarations describe PHP constants that may have no exact value.
:::

:::member[TYHP4194 (Error)]
**CheckerClassConstTypeRequired.** Message: <code>Class constant `{0}` must have a type annotation</code>.

Every class-level `const` needs a type, or inherits it from the ancestor that first declared the same name. A child `const X = 2;` under `const int X` is still `int`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4195 (Error)]
**CheckerClassConstTypeMismatch.** Message: <code>Class constant `{0}` type `{1}` must match inherited type `{2}`</code>.

Redeclaring a class constant cannot change its type. Omit the type to inherit it, or repeat the ancestor's type.
:::

:::member[TYHP4196 (Error)]
**CheckerForeachBindingTypeMismatch.** Message: <code>Foreach `{0}` type `{1}` is not assignable to declared type `{2}`</code>.

A foreach type annotation is a compatibility check, not a narrowing. The iterated key or value type must be assignable to the declared type; the loop variable then has that declared type.
:::

:::member[TYHP4197 (Error)]
**CheckerUnresolvedReceiver.** Message: <code>Cannot access a member, call a method, or index a value whose type could not be resolved</code>.

When the checker cannot type a receiver, that expression is marked unresolved so a missing name does not cascade through assignability. Member access, method calls (including extension lookup), and indexing still require a resolved type and report TYHP4197.

This diagnostic is omitted when the receiver subtree already has an error (for example `unknownFn()->x` reports only the undefined function). Unnarrowed `mixed` uses TYHP4160, not this code. Assignability of unresolved values is unchanged.
:::

:::member[TYHP4200 (Warning)]
**CheckerUnusedVariable.** Message: <code>Variable `${0}` is assigned but never read</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4200</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4201 (Warning)]
**CheckerUnusedParameter.** Message: <code>Parameter `${0}` is never used</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4201</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4202 (Warning)]
**CheckerUnusedPrivateMember.** Message: <code>Private member `{0}` is never referenced</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4202</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4203 (Warning)]
**CheckerAssignmentInCondition.** Message: <code>Assignment in condition; use `===` for comparison or add extra parentheses if intentional</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4203</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4204 (Warning)]
**CheckerConditionAlwaysTrueFalse.** Message: <code>Condition is always {0}</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4204</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4205 (Warning)]
**CheckerRedundantCast.** Message: <code>Redundant cast to `{0}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4205</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4206 (Warning)]
**CheckerDeadStore.** Message: <code>Value assigned to `${0}` is overwritten before being read</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4206</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4207 (Warning)]
**CheckerUnnecessaryNullCheck.** Message: <code>Unnecessary null check on non-nullable type `{0}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4207</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4208 (Warning)]
**CheckerUnreachableArm.** Message: <code>Unreachable match/switch arm</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4208</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4209 (Warning)]
**CheckerLossyCast.** Message: <code>Lossy cast from `{0}` to `{1}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4209</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4210 (Info)]
**CheckerErrorThresholdReached.** Message: <code>Error threshold reached for this file; further errors are suppressed</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4210</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4211 (Warning)]
**CheckerStaticReturnSelfInNonFinal.** Message: <code>Returning `new self()` from a method with return type `static` in non-final class `{0}`; child classes will receive parent instance</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4211</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4212 (Warning)]
**CheckerDisposableCircularReference.** Message: <code>Disposable scope has unresolvable circular references; disposal uses `try`/`finally` instead of `DisposableScope`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4212</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4213 (Error)]
**CheckerExistenceGateInvalidName.** Message: <code>Declaration existence gate must check for `{0}` (fully-qualified name or `__NAMESPACE__.&#39;\Name&#39;`)</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4213</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4300 (Error)]
**CheckerPhpVersionInvalidConstraint.** Message: <code>Invalid PHP version constraint `{0}`</code>.

The string given to `declare(php=…)` or `#[\Tyhp\Php]` is not a valid Composer PHP version constraint.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
declare(php="eight-four");
function demo(): void {}
```

Use Composer constraint syntax such as `>=8.4`, `^8.2`, `8.2.*`, or `>=8.2 <8.4`. A bare `"8.2"` means the whole `8.2.*` minor.
:::

:::member[TYHP4301 (Error)]
**CheckerPhpVersionDeclareNotAlone.** Message: <code>`declare(php=...)` must not be combined with other declare directives</code>.

The `php` version-gate directive must appear alone in its `declare` statement. Mixing it with `strict_types`, `output_file`, or any other key is rejected.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
declare(strict_types=1);
declare(php=">=8.4");
```

Write two consecutive `declare` statements instead of combining keys. Consecutive declares are valid.
:::

:::member[TYHP4302 (Error)]
**CheckerPhpVersionUnreachable.** Message: <code>Unreachable under PHP version constraint `{0}`</code>.

A nested PHP version constraint can never be true given its enclosing constraint, so the inner region is unreachable.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
declare(php=">=8.4") {
    function outer(): void {}

    declare(php="<8.3") {
        function never(): void {}
    }
}
```

This error applies only to nested gates. Sibling `declare(php=…)` blocks that cover different PHP versions are alternate variants, not unreachable code. An inactive file-level `declare(php="…");` skips the file silently and does not report this error.
:::

:::member[TYHP4303 (Error)]
**CheckerPhpVersionDuplicateDeclaration.** Message: <code>Duplicate declaration of `{0}` with overlapping PHP version constraints</code>.

Duplicate declarations of the same symbol have overlapping PHP version constraints. Two variants of a name are allowed when their effective constraints are pairwise disjoint, or when they are distinct function or method overloads (different parameter lists) under the same or overlapping gates.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
#[\Tyhp\Php(">=8.3")]
function example(): void {}

#[\Tyhp\Php(">=8.4")]
function example(): void {}
```

Those two constraints both match PHP 8.4 and later. Use disjoint ranges such as `>=8.4` with `<8.4` when you need version-specific declarations of the same name and signature.
:::

:::member[TYHP4304 (Error)]
**CheckerPhpVersionAttributeInvalidTarget.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\Php]` is not allowed on struct or extension declarations; wrap with `declare(php=...)` instead</code>.

`#[\Tyhp\Php]` is not a valid attribute target on a `struct` or on a Tyhp or tyhpdef `extension` declaration. Gate those forms with `declare(php=…)` instead.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
declare(php=">=8.4") {
    extension GatedStringOps {
        function gated_tag(extends string $this): string {
            return \strtoupper($this);
        }
    }
}
```

The attribute remains legal on class, interface, enum, trait, their members, functions, and other ordinary attribute targets. File-level `declare(php="…");` also gates the rest of that file.
:::

:::member[TYHP4305 (Error)]
**CheckerPhpVersionAttributeInvalidArgument.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\Php]` requires a string `version` argument</code>.

`#[\Tyhp\Php]` requires a string `version` argument, either positional or named. Omitting it, or passing a non-string, is rejected.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
#[\Tyhp\Php(">=8.4")]
function array_find(array $array, callable $callback): mixed {
    return null;
}

#[\Tyhp\Php(version: ">=8.2 <8.4")]
function example(string $v): mixed {
    return $v;
}
```

On a tyhpdef hooked property, place `#[\Tyhp\Php]` on the property, not on `get` or `set`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4306 (Warning)]
**CheckerPhpVersionDefaulted.** Message: <code>`output.phpVersion` is unset; defaulting to `8.2`</code>.

The compile target was defaulted to `"8.2"` because no project `phpVersion` was set, and this warning is emitted once per compilation.

Set `output.phpVersion` in `tyhp.json` to an explicit `"8.0"`–`"8.5"` value to choose the check and emit target and which version-gated declarations are visible. This diagnostic fires once per compilation, not once per file. An explicit but unsupported value is a different diagnostic and falls back to `"8.4"`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4307 (Error)]
**CheckerExternTypeUsed.** Message: <code>Name `{0}` is extern</code>.

A `.tyhp` file named or received an `extern` name. That name is a tyhpdef placeholder for a type, function, or const the current tyhpdef mentions but does not own, so it is not usable in Tyhp source.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function f(\Elastica\Client $client): void {}
\bcadd("1", "2");
int $mode = \GMP_ROUND_PLUSINF;
```

The primary span is the use: a type annotation, `new`, `instanceof`, `catch`, a `use` / `use function` / `use const` import of that fully-qualified name, a generic argument, a union or intersection arm, a call of an extern function, a const fetch, or an expression whose inferred type is extern (including a call whose return or parameter type is extern). A secondary span labeled "declared here" points at the `extern` declaration.

When the declaration has `// @provided-by: tyhpdef/ruflin-elastica` or `// @provided-by: tyhpdef/php-ext-bcmath`, help cites that wrapper name as-is. Include that package so a real declaration replaces the placeholder.

Naming a real class whose signature mentions an extern type is not itself a use. Tyhpdef signatures and mapping bodies may name an extern function or const.
:::

:::member[TYHP4310 (Error)]
**CheckerGenericDefaultDoesNotSatisfyConstraint.** Message: <code>Default type `{0}` does not satisfy constraint `{1}` on generic parameter `{2}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4310</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4311 (Error)]
**CheckerGenericNonDefaultAfterDefault.** Message: <code>Generic parameter `{0}` without a default cannot follow parameter `{1}` which has a default</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4311</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4312 (Error)]
**CheckerGenericDefaultCircularReference.** Message: <code>Generic parameter `{0}` has a circular default type reference</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4312</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4320 (Error)]
**CheckerPropertyPathRequiresInlineFn.** Message: <code>Parameter of type `PropertyPath&lt;callable({0}): {1}&gt;` requires an inline fn expression (e.g., fn ($x) =&gt; $x-&gt;property)</code>.

A value that is not an inline `fn` was passed where `PropertyPath<callable(TSource $source): TReturn>` is expected. The compiler reads the property chain out of the arrow function at compile time, so an already-built closure carries no chain it can lower.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function takes(\Tyhp\PropertyPath<callable(User $u): string> $path): void {}

takes($someClosure);
```

Pass an inline arrow function instead — `takes(fn ($u) => $u->name)`. Forwarding an existing `PropertyPath` value (for example a parameter of the same type) is also accepted.
:::

:::member[TYHP4321 (Error)]
**CheckerPropertyPathInvalidBody.** Message: <code>PropertyPath expression must be a simple property access chain (e.g., fn ($x) =&gt; $x-&gt;prop-&gt;subProp)</code>.

The inline `fn` body is not a simple property-access chain rooted at the lambda parameter. Method calls, operators, function wrappers, and roots other than the parameter cannot be represented as a property path.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function takes(\Tyhp\PropertyPath<callable(User $u): string> $path): void {}

takes(fn ($u) => \strtolower($u->name));
```

Use only `->` or `?->` property accesses starting at the parameter — `takes(fn ($u) => $u->address->city)`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4322 (Error)]
**CheckerExpressionUnsupportedNode.** Message: <code>Expression trees do not support `{0}` expressions; simplify the fn body</code>.

The inline `fn` body contains an expression kind that cannot be represented in an expression tree. The message names the construct in words, for example `function call`, `array literal`, `first-class callable`, `shell command`, `string interpolation`, `assignment`, `match`, `nested fn`, `await`, or `isset`. These constructs are rejected so the emitted tree stays a faithful, inspectable data structure. See [Parsable Lambdas and Expression Trees](tyhp_3000_parsableLambdas.md#unsupported-expression-types) for the full list.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function takes(\Tyhp\Expression<callable(User $u): bool> $pred): void {}

takes(fn ($u) => await $u->load());
```

Simplify the body to supported forms: property/method access, operators, casts, ternary/`??`, array access, `new`, `instanceof`/`is`, literals, and definitely-assigned captures.
:::

:::member[TYHP4323 (Error)]
**CheckerExpressionRequiresInlineFn.** Message: <code>Parameter of type `Expression&lt;callable({0}): {1}&gt;` requires an inline fn expression</code>.

A value that is not an inline `fn` was passed where `Expression<callable(T $arg): R>` is expected. The compiler builds the expression tree from the arrow function at compile time, so an already-built closure carries no tree it can lower.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function takes(\Tyhp\Expression<callable(User $u): bool> $pred): void {}

takes($someClosure);
```

Pass an inline arrow function instead — `takes(fn ($u) => $u->age > 18)`. Forwarding an existing `Expression` value (for example a parameter of the same type) is also accepted.
:::

:::member[TYHP4324 (Error)]
**CheckerExpressionCapturedVarUndefined.** Message: <code>Captured variable `${0}` in expression tree must be definitely assigned</code>.

A variable from the enclosing scope is referenced inside an expression-tree `fn`, so it becomes a `ConstantExpression` capture. That variable must be definitely assigned at the construction site; reading an uninitialized local would produce an undefined runtime value in the tree.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function takes(\Tyhp\Expression<callable(User $u): bool> $pred): void {}

function demo(): void {
    int $minAge;
    takes(fn ($u) => $u->age > $minAge);
}
```

Assign the captured variable before constructing the expression — `$minAge = 18;` then `takes(fn ($u) => $u->age > $minAge)`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4325 (Error)]
**CheckerStructRequiredKeyMissing.** Message: <code>Required struct property `{0}` is missing from `{1}`</code>.

A required field of a callable-parameter bag (`__CallableParametersStruct` / `__CallableParametersTuple`) is missing from the array literal. Parameters without defaults are required struct keys; parameters with defaults are optional keys and may be omitted.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function apply<TCallable extends callable>(
    TCallable $cb,
    __CallableParametersStruct<TCallable> $args
): __CallableReturnType<TCallable> {
    return $cb();
}

function greet(string $name, int $age = 0): string {
    return $name;
}

function demo(): void {
    apply(greet(...), ['name' => 'Ada']);
    apply(greet(...), []);
}
```

The first call is valid (`$age` has a default). The second is not — `$name` is required. Optionality is modeled as required-key assignability on one struct, not an intersection of every key-subset bag.
:::

:::member[TYHP4326 (Error)]
**CheckerTraversableCannotBeListed.** Message: <code>`{0}` cannot list `\Traversable`; use `\Iterator` or `\IteratorAggregate`</code>.

`\Traversable` is an engine interface. Only `\Iterator` and `\IteratorAggregate` may extend it. Classes, enums, interfaces, and traits list `\Iterator` or `\IteratorAggregate` instead of `\Traversable`. Listing both (for example `implements \Iterator, \Traversable`) is also rejected.
:::

:::member[TYHP4327 (Error)]
**CheckerPhpTypeInvalidTarget.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\PhpType]` is not allowed on `{0}`</code>.

`#[\Tyhp\PhpType]` replaces the emitted PHP type of a parameter, function or method return, property, or typed constant. It is not a valid target on a class, interface, trait, enum, enum case, catch type, local variable, or property hook. Put the attribute on the property or on the `set` parameter instead of on `get`/`set`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4328 (Error)]
**CheckerGeneratorSendIntersectionEmpty.** Message: <code>Generator `TSend` intersection of `{0}` is empty</code>.

Each typed use of a `yield` expression (for example `int $x = yield` or `foo(yield)` when `foo` takes `int`) constrains generator `TSend` — the type of `Generator::send()`. Several such targets are intersected. If that intersection is empty (for example `int` vs `string`), no send value can satisfy every site. Untyped `$x = yield` does not constrain `TSend` (it stays `mixed`).
:::

:::member[TYHP4329 (Error)]
**CheckerPhpTypeInvalidSpelling.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\PhpType]` argument `{0}` is not a valid PHP type hint</code>.

`#[\Tyhp\PhpType]` takes a PHP type-hint spelling such as `mixed`, `int`, `string|int`, or `?\Foo`. The constructor argument must be that string; invalid spelling (for example `int[]`, `?mixed`, or a missing argument) is a compile error. Checker types are unchanged; only the emitted PHP type uses the hint.
:::

:::member[TYHP4330 (Error)]
**CheckerArrayAccessKeyNotOffset.** Message: <code>`ArrayAccess` key type `{0}` cannot be a struct or array</code>.

PHP array offsets cannot be arrays. Tyhp structs erase to arrays, so `ArrayAccess<SomeStruct, TValue>` is not a legal homogeneous map (that spelling is `TKey` plus default `TValue`, not a per-key shape). Use `int`, `string`, `int|string`, or an object key type. Per-key struct maps are `ArrayAccessShape`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4331 (Error)]
**CheckerArrayAccessShapeWideKey.** Message: <code>`ArrayAccessShape` key type `{0}` is too wide; narrow or use `as`</code>.

An `ArrayAccessShape` index must be a struct-key literal (or a finite union of those keys). A wide `string`, `int`, or `mixed` key is not enough; narrow the key or assert it with `as`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4332 (Error)]
**CheckerArrayAccessShapeAppend.** Message: <code>`ArrayAccessShape` does not allow append (`$obj[] =`)</code>.

`ArrayAccessShape` has a closed key set from `TStruct`. Append (`$obj[] =`) is only legal on homogeneous `ArrayAccess`. Write a known key such as `$obj['host'] = …`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4333 (Error)]
**CheckerArrayAccessShapeUnhandledKey.** Message: <code>`ArrayAccessShape` key `{0}` is not covered by `{1}`</code>.

For each finite struct key `K`, `offsetGet` / `offsetSet` is checked with `$offset` assumed `K`. A key is covered only by a reachable value return (`offsetGet`) or a write of `$value` (`offsetSet`) of that field's type. `throw` and `never` do not cover an unhandled key; `match` is sufficient but not required.
:::

:::member[TYHP4334 (Error)]
**CheckerClosureBindIncompatible.** Message: <code>Cannot bind this closure to `{0}`; expected `{1}`</code>.

After `bindTo($x)` or `bindTo($x, 'static')` the leftover `TScope` is unchanged. `$newThis` must still be an instance of that scope class (or of `TThis` when the stored scope is gradual). An explicit object `$newScope` requires `TNewThis` to be a subtype of that object's type; a string `$newScope` must be `__SuperTypeName<TNewThis>` (an ancestor name, not a descendant). `call($newThis)` is a temporary bind: `$newThis` must be a non-null object compatible the same way. Gradual `TThis` (`object|null` / bare `\Closure`) does not prove an error.
:::

:::member[TYHP4335 (Error)]
**CheckerClosureStaticScopeStored.** Message: <code>`&#39;static&#39;` is not a stored closure `TScope`; it is only a `bind` / `bindTo` argument</code>.

The token `'static'` on `bind` / `bindTo` means "keep the old stored `TScope`". It is not a class-name string and must not appear as a Closure type argument. Write `\Closure<callable(…): mixed, TThis, TScope>` with a real scope type, or omit `TScope` so the default `__ClosureScope<TThis>` is used.
:::

:::member[TYHP4336 (Error)]
**CheckerClosureNonRebindable.** Message: <code>This closure cannot be rebound</code>.

PHP refuses to rebind some closures. Arrow functions, first-class callables, and `fromCallable` of a non-Closure cannot change `$this` or scope. Binding `$newThis` or `$newScope` to an internal (engine) class is also forbidden. A gradual `\Closure` annotation does not prove the value is non-rebindable.
:::

:::member[TYHP4337 (Error)]
**CheckerEngineEnumCannotBeListed.** Message: <code>`{0}` cannot list `{1}`</code>.

`\UnitEnum` and `\BackedEnum` are engine interfaces. Classes, interfaces, and traits cannot implement or extend them. Enumerations are already `\UnitEnum` (and `\BackedEnum` when backed) and must not list those interfaces in `implements`. Only `\BackedEnum` may extend `\UnitEnum`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4338 (Error)]
**CheckerEnumEngineMethodRedeclared.** Message: <code>`{0}` cannot redeclare `{1}`</code>.

The engine supplies `cases` on every enumeration and `from` / `tryFrom` on backed enumerations. Redeclaring those methods is an error.
:::

:::member[TYHP4339 (Error)]
**CheckerOverrideOnConstructor.** Message: <code>`#[Override]` cannot be applied to `__construct`</code>.

PHP constructors are exempt from override signature checks, so `#[Override]` is invalid on `__construct` even when a parent constructor exists. This error is reported at every `output.phpVersion`. Use `#[Override]` on methods or (PHP 8.5 or later) properties that actually replace a parent or interface member. A method or property that does not override uses TYHP4129 instead.
:::

:::member[TYHP4340 (Error)]
**CheckerNativeTypeTestInvalidTarget.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\NativeTypeTest]` is not allowed on `{0}`</code>.

`#[\Tyhp\NativeTypeTest]` marks a free function or concrete static method as the native lowering for `$x is T`. Instance methods, abstract or interface methods, closures, and other declarations cannot be that lowering; emit is `fqn($x)` or `\Class::method($x)` with the guarded first parameter.
:::

:::member[TYHP4341 (Error)]
**CheckerNativeTypeTestRequiresTypeGuard.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\NativeTypeTest]` requires a type-guard return `{0} is T` on the first parameter</code>.

The attribute does not take a type argument. `T` is the type-guard return of the same function: the first parameter must be named in `$param is T` (not `$other is T` and not an index subject such as `$array[$key] is T`).
:::

:::member[TYHP4342 (Error)]
**CheckerNativeTypeTestTypeNotSingle.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\NativeTypeTest]` type `{0}` must be a single type; unions, intersections, and nullables are not allowed</code>.

`T` must be a single type after transparent alias expansion. Unions (`int|string`), intersections, and nullables (`?string`) stay on `\Tyhp\Type::is` at `$x is …` sites; mark a guard only when it tests one exact type (for example `string`, `int`, or a class name).
:::

:::member[TYHP4343 (Error)]
**CheckerNativeTypeTestExtraParamsNeedDefaults.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\NativeTypeTest]` extra parameters after the first must have default values</code>.

`$x is T` emits `fqn($x)` and does not pass further arguments. Extra parameters after the guarded first parameter must all have defaults (or be variadic) so a one-argument call is valid.
:::

:::member[TYHP4344 (Error)]
**CheckerNativeTypeTestDuplicate.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\NativeTypeTest]` for `{0}` overlaps `{1}` registered by `{2}`</code>.

Only one callable may be the native test for a given `T`, including overlapping guarded types (for example `string` and `int|float|string`). Canonical PHP builtins such as `is_int` are marked; aliases such as `is_integer` / `is_long` stay callable but do not win `$x is int`. Concrete static methods are allowed; instance and abstract methods are not.
:::

:::member[TYHP4345 (Error)]
**CheckerEraseGenericInvalidTarget.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\EraseGeneric]` is not allowed on `{0}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4345</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4346 (Warning)]
**CheckerGenericRuntimeAuthorWritten.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\GenericRuntime]` is compiler-generated; this usage is overwritten at emit</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4346</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4347 (Error)]
**CheckerObjectShapeUsedAsClass.** Message: <code>Object shape `{0}` is not a class</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4347</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4348 (Error)]
**CheckerObjectShapeNotTypeAlias.** Message: <code>`object { }` is only allowed as the right-hand side of a `type` alias</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4348</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4349 (Error)]
**CheckerObjectShapeEmpty.** Message: <code>Empty object shape is not allowed; use `object`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4349</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4350 (Error)]
**CheckerObjectShapeNonPublicMember.** Message: <code>Object shape member `{0}` must be `public`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4350</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4351 (Error)]
**CheckerNewTypeArgumentNotObjectShape.** Message: <code>Type argument `{0}` of `__New` must be an object-shape alias</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4351</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4352 (Error)]
**CheckerNewConstraintNotConstructable.** Message: <code>`{0}` does not satisfy `__New&lt;{1}&gt;` because it is `{2}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4352</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4353 (Error)]
**CheckerNewConstraintNonPublicConstructor.** Message: <code>`{0}` does not satisfy `__New&lt;{1}&gt;` because its constructor is not `public`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4353</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4354 (Error)]
**CheckerNewConstraintConstructorMismatch.** Message: <code>`{0}` does not satisfy `__New&lt;{1}&gt;` because its constructor is not compatible</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4354</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4355 (Error)]
**CheckerNewTypeParameterRequiresNew.** Message: <code>`new {0}()` requires `{0}` to be `__New&lt;...&gt;`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4355</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4356 (Error)]
**CheckerNewClassNameRequiresNew.** Message: <code>`new ${0}()` requires `__ClassName&lt;__New&lt;...&gt;&gt;`, found `{1}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4356</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4357 (Error)]
**CheckerObjectShapeConstructorArgumentMismatch.** Message: <code>Constructor arguments for `{0}` do not match object shape `{1}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4357</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4358 (Error)]
**CheckerObjectShapeRequiresGuard.** Message: <code>`{0}` is not assignable to object shape `{1}` without a shape guard</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4358</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4359 (Error)]
**CheckerObjectShapeConstructNotCallable.** Message: <code>`__construct` is not callable on a value of object shape `{0}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4359</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4360 (Error)]
**CheckerCallableShapeRequiresGuard.** Message: <code>`{0}` is not assignable to callable shape `{1}` without a shape guard</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4360</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4361 (Error)]
**ParserExtensionLegacyMemberTarget.** Message: <code>Per-member `extends Type $this` and `operator op&lt;Type&gt;` are not how an extension names its target. Use `extension Name extends Type` or a nested `extends Type` group</code>.

Writing `extends Type $this` on a member, or `<Type>` after an operator token, is the old per-member target spelling. Name the target on the block with `extension Name extends Type` or a nested `extends Type` group. Adaptation clauses in `use extension` still qualify an operator by target (`E::operator +<Money>`).
:::

:::member[TYHP4362 (Error)]
**CheckerExtensionHeaderAndNestedTargets.** Message: <code>Extension `{0}` declares a header `extends` and a nested `extends` group</code>.

A header `extends` and nested `extends` groups are mutually exclusive. A header `extends Type` covers every member of the extension. Nested `extends Type { }` groups each name their own target in place of a header. Keep one header target, or move every member into a group.
:::

:::member[TYHP4363 (Error)]
**CheckerExtensionLooseMemberBesideGroup.** Message: <code>Extension `{0}` declares a nested `extends` group and a member outside a group</code>.

An extension that uses nested `extends` groups puts every member inside a group. A member written beside those groups, outside any group, has no target. Move the member into a group, or remove the groups and use a header `extends` for the whole extension.
:::

:::member[TYHP4364 (Error)]
**CheckerExtensionTargetNotSingleType.** Message: <code>Expected a single named type, found `{0}`</code>.

The block target is an intersection, `void`, `never`, `mixed`, a type parameter, an `object { … }` shape, `_`, or a union that contains one of those. A union whose members are each a legal target is valid, and so is `?T`. An alias is read through to its body, so an alias of a legal union is a legal target.
:::

:::member[TYHP4365 (Error)]
**CheckerExtensionUnusedTypeParameter.** Message: <code>Type parameter `{0}` is not used</code>.

A type parameter on `extension Name<T>` or on a nested `extends<T>` group is in scope for that block and must be referenced there: in the target, in a constraint or default, or in a member. A parameter that is never referenced is unused. Remove it, or use it.
:::

:::member[TYHP4366 (Error)]
**CheckerExtensionTypeParameterShadowed.** Message: <code>Type parameter `{0}` shadows a type parameter on the enclosing extension</code>.

Type parameters on `extension Name<T>` or `extends<T>` stay on that symbol. They are in scope for the target and the members, and they are not copied onto each method. A method lists only the type parameters written on it. A method type parameter that reuses one of those names shadows the enclosing parameter. Give the method parameter a different name.
:::

:::member[TYHP4367 (Error)]
**CheckerExtensionOverlappingMember.** Message: <code>`{0}` is declared on overlapping targets `{1}` and `{2}`</code>.

Two groups in one extension overlap when both can apply to the same receiver and both declare the same method or operator. `extends string` and `extends string|int` both apply to `string`. Different member names on overlapping targets are fine. Targets that do not overlap may share a method name. The same member on two separate extensions is an activation conflict, resolved with `hide` or `insteadof` on `use extension`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4368 (Error)]
**CheckerExtensionRelativeType.** Message: <code>`{0}::` is not allowed in an extension member</code>.

Inside an extension member, `self` and `self::` name the block target, including a scalar target. `static::` and `parent::` are not the block target. Name the extension class by writing its name. An anonymous class nested in the member keeps its own `self` and `static`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4369 (Error)]
**CheckerExtensionByRefReceiverRequired.** Message: <code>Extension member `{0}` writes `$this` without `&amp;$this`</code>.

An extension member that writes `$this` needs the `&$this` receiver annotation. A write is an assignment, a compound assignment, `++` / `--`, or passing `$this` to a by-reference parameter. On a class, interface, or enum, assigning a property (`$this->amount = 1`) or calling a method does not write `$this`. On a scalar, array, or struct, assigning through `$this` (`$this->field`, `$this[$k]`, or `$this[]`) does.
:::

:::member[TYHP4370 (Error)]
**CheckerExtensionByRefReceiverUnused.** Message: <code>Extension member `{0}` declares `&amp;$this` but does not write `$this`</code>.

`&$this` is the by-reference receiver annotation, and an extension member declares it only when the body writes `$this`. Reading `$this`, or mutating a property of a class, interface, or enum receiver, is not that write. Remove `&$this`, or write `$this` if the annotation was intentional. A missing annotation on a member that does write `$this` is `TYHP4369`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4371 (Error)]
**CheckerPhpVersionAttributeInvalidMember.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\Php]` is not allowed on `{0}`; declare a separate type per PHP version inside `declare(php=...)` instead</code>.

PHP cannot declare a property, class constant, enum case, or interface method conditionally, so `#[\Tyhp\Php]` on one of them has no PHP form to emit. When such a member differs between PHP versions, declare the whole class, interface, or enum once per version inside `declare(php=…)` blocks.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
declare(php="<8.3") {
    class Limits {
        const MAX = 10;
    }
}

declare(php=">=8.3") {
    class Limits {
        const int MAX = 10;
    }
}
```

`#[\Tyhp\Php]` stays legal on functions, classes, interfaces, traits, enums, and methods of classes, traits, and enums. Members of tyhpdef declarations may still carry it.
:::

:::member[TYHP4372 (Error)]
**CheckerReservedPhp86Name.** Message: <code>The name `{0}` cannot be used as a `{1}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4372</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP4373 (Error)]
**CheckerAwaitedBoundNotSettled.** Message: <code>Type argument `{0}` for `{1}` must be an already-awaited type (not a promise, a union with a promise member, or a type parameter that could hold one, such as an unconstrained one or one bounded by `mixed`); use a settled type, or constrain the type parameter with `extends __Awaited&lt;…&gt;`</code>.

A type parameter declared `T extends __Awaited<…>` holds only a type that is its own awaited type, so `Promise<T>` can never be a promise of a promise. `Promise<Promise<int>>`, `Promise<int|Promise<string>>`, and `Promise<T>` for an unconstrained `T` (or a `T` bounded only by `mixed` or `object`) are rejected, because such a `T` could itself be a promise. `Promise<mixed>` and `Promise<object>` are accepted. Use the settled type (`Promise<int>`), or constrain your own type parameter the same way:

```tyhp
<?tyhp
function collect<T extends __Awaited<void|mixed>>(array<Promise<T>> $promises): array<T> {
    // ...
}
```
:::

:::member[TYHP4374 (Error)]
**CheckerOverloadNoMatch.** Message: <code>No overload of `{0}` matches this call. Overloads: {1}</code>.

A call to an overloaded function or method must match one of the declared overload signatures; the implementation's own signature is not callable. The first signature, in declaration order, whose parameters accept the arguments as written is used. Only when none does are the signatures tried again with the implicit `operator convert` conversions an ordinary call applies (see TYHP4375). If no signature accepts the arguments even with those conversions, the error lists every signature.

A callable value such as `$fn = describe(...)` is called through the signatures it was created from: `$fn(5)` is accepted when an argument fits a signature as written, or when it is a type that converts implicitly to that signature's parameter at that position (see TYHP4376). Any other argument reports this error, listing the signatures.
:::

:::member[TYHP4375 (Error)]
**CheckerOverloadAmbiguous.** Message: <code>The call to `{0}` is ambiguous: no overload accepts the arguments as written, and more than one accepts them only through implicit conversion to different types. Overloads: {1}. Convert an argument explicitly (for example with a cast) to choose one</code>.

When no overload accepts a call as written, the compiler tries the overloads again, allowing the implicit `operator convert` conversions an ordinary call applies (class-owned and extension conversions, and conversion to a scalar such as `int`, unless the conversion is hidden with `operator convert hide`). If several overloads accept the call only through conversion, they are narrowed in two steps:

1. An overload that converts only some of the arguments another overload converts, and converts those to the same types, is preferred over it.
2. Among the remaining overloads, if they all convert the arguments to the same types, the first declared is used. If they convert to different types, the call is ambiguous.

Convert the argument yourself (for example `new Money(5)`) so that one overload accepts it as written, and the ambiguity disappears.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
final class Money {
    public function __construct(public int $cents) {}
    operator convert(int $value) { return new self($value); }
}

final class Meters {
    public function __construct(public int $value) {}
    operator convert(int $value) { return new self($value); }
}

function measure(Money $m): string;
function measure(Meters $m): string;
function measure(Money|Meters $a): string {
    return 'measured';
}

function run(): void {
    echo measure(5);             // error: both overloads need a conversion of 5
    echo measure(new Money(5));  // OK: accepted as written
}
```
:::

:::member[TYHP4376 (Error)]
**CheckerOverloadCallableAmbiguousConversion.** Message: <code>The first-class callable `{0}(...)` cannot convert a `{1}` argument at position {2}: no overload accepts it as written, and the overloads convert it to different types (`{3}`). Call the overload directly, or pass an argument that one overload accepts</code>.

A first-class callable of an overloaded function or method converts its arguments the way an ordinary call does, one parameter position at a time. At each position:

- A type that some overload accepts as written there is passed as it is.
- Any other type that converts implicitly to an overload's parameter is converted to it, and the callable accepts that type.
- A type that would convert to a *different* type in different overloads cannot be converted, because the callable does not know which overload the caller means.

This error reports the third case, at the `(...)` of the first-class callable. Call the overload directly with an argument that one overload accepts, or give the overloads the same parameter type at that position.

```tyhp
<?tyhp
final class Money {
    public function __construct(public int $cents) {}
    operator convert(int $value) { return new self($value); }
}

final class Meters {
    public function __construct(public int $value) {}
    operator convert(int $value) { return new self($value); }
}

function measure(Money $m): string;
function measure(Meters $m): string;
function measure(Money|Meters $a): string {
    return 'measured';
}

$fn = measure(...); // error: an int converts to Money and to Meters
```
:::

:::member[TYHP4377 (Error)]
**CheckerCannotInferTypeArgument.** Message: <code>Cannot infer type argument `{0}` for `{1}`. Specify it explicitly</code>.

A generic call whose type parameter is not fixed by an explicit type argument, by the arguments, or by the type expected at the call (the variable, parameter, or return the call is used as) uses the parameter's declared default. When there is no default either, the call reports this error. Write the type argument explicitly (`make<int>()`).

```tyhp
<?tyhp
class Box<T> {
    public function __construct(public ?T $value = null) {}
}
function make<T>(): Box<T> { return new Box<T>(); }
function makeD<T = int>(): Box<T> { return new Box<T>(); }

function demo(): void {
    $a = make();            // error: T cannot be inferred
    Box<int> $b = make();   // T is int, from the variable type
    Box<int> $c = makeD();  // T is int, the declared default
}
```
:::

:::member[TYHP4500 (Warning)]
**CheckerDeprecatedUsage.** Message: <code>`{0}` is deprecated{1}</code>.

A use of a deprecated symbol. The compiler sets deprecation from `#[\Deprecated]` on the declaration and from the tyhpdef `deprecated` keyword. Both produce this same warning (TYHP4500).

When `#[\Deprecated]` has a string-literal `$message`, that text is appended after a colon. `$since` is not part of the short message.

The symbol still compiles. Tyhp warns even when `output.phpVersion` is below 8.4 (PHP's runtime `E_USER_DEPRECATED` is a no-op on older minors). The class itself stays version-gated in `tyhpdef/php`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4501 (Error)]
**CheckerObsoleteUsage.** Message: <code>`{0}` is obsolete and must not be used</code>.

Code references a symbol that has been marked as obsolete. This is stronger than deprecated and the symbol may be removed imminently.
:::

:::member[TYHP4800 (Info)]
**CheckerEvalUsage.** Message: <code>`eval()` usage detected — this is disabled in Tyhp by default</code>.

The code uses `eval()`, which Tyhp disallows by default for security and type-safety reasons.

Fix: Replace `eval()` with a safer alternative. If `eval()` is absolutely necessary, enable it with `build.allowEval: true` in `tyhp.json`.
:::

:::member[TYHP4801 (Error)]
**CheckerIncludeNotAllowed.** Message: <code>`include`/`require` is not allowed in Tyhp; use `import` instead</code>.

Tyhp does not allow `include`, `require`, `include_once`, or `require_once` statements. Use `use`/`import` statements and Composer autoloading instead.
:::

:::member[TYHP4802 (Error)]
**CheckerNestedNamedFunctionNotAllowed.** Message: <code>Named function or method `{0}` cannot be declared inside another function or method; nested named declarations are not allowed in Tyhp</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP4802</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::


## Emitter Errors (TYHP5xxx)

Emitter errors occur during PHP code generation.

:::member[TYHP5001 (Error)]
**EmitterUnknownError.** Message: <code>Unknown emitter error: {0}</code>.

A catch-all for unexpected errors during PHP code generation.
:::

:::member[TYHP5002 (Error)]
**EmitterUnsupportedAstNode.** Message: <code>Cannot emit AST node type `{0}` — no emission handler implemented</code>.

The emitter encountered an AST node type that it does not know how to convert to PHP. This typically indicates a new language feature whose emitter support is not yet complete.
:::

:::member[TYHP5003 (Error)]
**EmitterOutputPathConflict.** Message: <code>Output path conflict: `{0}` is targeted by multiple declarations</code>.

Two or more class/file declarations would produce output at the same file path.

Fix: Ensure each class has a unique fully-qualified name. If two classes share a name, place them in different namespaces.
:::

:::member[TYHP5004 (Error)]
**EmitterNamespaceMismatch.** Message: <code>Cannot merge output files: namespace mismatch (`{0}` vs `{1}`)</code>.

An attempt to merge two output files failed because they declare different namespaces.
:::

:::member[TYHP5005 (Error)]
**EmitterInvalidOutputPath.** Message: <code>Invalid output path: `{0}` — {1}</code>.

The computed output path for a generated PHP file is invalid or inaccessible.
:::

:::member[TYHP5006 (Warning)]
**EmitterTypeErasureWarning.** Message: <code>Type `{0}` is erased to `mixed` in PHP output</code>.

A Tyhp type could not be represented in PHP and was erased to `mixed`. This is informational -- the type checking was still performed at compile time.
:::

:::member[TYHP5007 (Error)]
**EmitterWriteError.** Message: <code>Failed to write output file `{0}`: {1}</code>.

The emitter could not write a generated PHP file to disk due to a file system error.
:::

:::member[TYHP5008 (Warning)]
**EmitterTyhpConstructNotImplemented.** Message: <code>Tyhp construct `{0}` is not yet supported by the emitter</code>.

A Tyhp-specific language feature does not yet have emitter support. The code compiles but the feature is not emitted.
:::

:::member[TYHP5009 (Error)]
**EmitterInvalidDeclareDirective.** Message: <code>Invalid declare directive: {0}</code>.

A `declare()` statement contains an invalid or conflicting directive.
:::

:::member[TYHP5010 (Warning)]
**EmitterEmptyOutputFile.** Message: <code>Output file `{0}` has no statements and will not be written</code>.

An output file was generated with no PHP statements (e.g., a source file contained only type aliases or struct declarations that are erased).
:::

:::member[TYHP5011 (Warning)]
**EmitterMergeConflict.** Message: <code>Conflicting declarations during merge of `{0}`: {1}</code>.

Two output files being merged into one contain conflicting declarations.
:::

:::member[TYHP5012 (Error)]
**EmitterUnsupportedConstruct.** Message: <code>Tyhp construct `{0}` cannot be emitted to PHP</code>.

An unsupported Tyhp construct cannot be lowered to PHP — it is not merely unimplemented yet (that is TYHP5008). The emitter has no valid PHP representation for the named construct.

Fix: Rewrite the code using a construct Tyhp can emit, or check whether a newer compiler adds support.
:::

:::member[TYHP5013 (Error)]
**EmitterNameConflict.** Message: <code>Generated method name `{0}` conflicts with an existing method in `{1}`</code>.

A method name the emitter generated (for example a lowered hook, generic variant, or helper) conflicts with a method that already exists on the same class.

Fix: Rename the authored method so it does not clash with the generated name.
:::

:::member[TYHP5014 (Error)]
**EmitterMissingRuntime.** Message: <code>TyhpLib runtime is required but not configured for `{0}`</code>.

The compiled output needs the TyhpLib runtime (the `tyhp/core` family of packages) for the named construct, but the project is not configured to include it.

Fix: Restore the runtime package reference (Composer `tyhp/core` / `tyhp.json` runtime settings) and rebuild.
:::

:::member[TYHP5016 (Error)]
**EmitterDisposableError.** Message: <code>Disposable variable of type `{0}` does not implement `IsDisposable`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP5016</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP5017 (Warning)]
**EmitterAttributeStrippedForPhpVersion.** Message: <code>Attribute `{0}` on `{1}` is stripped; target PHP `{2}` cannot represent it</code>.

PHP only allows attributes on certain constructs starting at specific versions. Top-level (non-class) `const` attributes require PHP 8.5+. Attributes on property hooks require native property hooks (PHP 8.4+); when hooks are lowered for an older `output.phpVersion`, those attributes cannot be preserved in a Reflection-compatible form.

Raise `output.phpVersion`, or remove the attribute if it is not needed at runtime.
:::

:::member[TYHP5018 (Error)]
**EmitterInteropContractMismatch.** Message: <code>Runtime package `{0}` interop contract version is `{1}`, expected `{2}`</code>.

Compiled Tyhp depends on concrete `\Tyhp\*` runtime shapes. Each runtime Composer package stamps `extra.tyhp.interopContractVersion`, which must match the compiler's `InteropContract.CurrentVersion`.

Upgrade or reinstall matching `tyhp/core`, `tyhp/async`, `tyhp/decimal`, and/or `tyhp/lambda` packages, or upgrade the Tyhp compiler so both sides share the same contract version. See the interop contract docs.
:::

:::member[TYHP5019 (Error)]
**EmitterPostfixOperatorOverloadRequiresStatementSplit.** Message: <code>Overloaded postfix `{0}` cannot be statement-split in this expression; capture the prior value in a separate statement</code>.

Overloaded `++` / `--` rewrites to a method call plus write-back. Postfix forms must yield the value from before that write-back, which the emitter does by splitting into preceding statements (`$__old = $a; $a = Type::__increment($a);` … `$__old`).

That split is not safe inside short-circuit operands (`&&`, `||`, `??`), ternary arms, `else if` conditions (reached only when earlier conditions in the chain were false), or loop conditions that re-evaluate each iteration. Move the postfix into its own statement (or use prefix `++$a` when the new value is intended), then use the captured variable in the expression.
:::

:::member[TYHP5020 (Warning)]
**EmitterSourceMapGenerationFailed.** Message: <code>Failed to generate source map for file `{0}`: {1}</code>.

Source map generation builds Source Map v3 JSON from mappings collected while emitting PHP. A failure here is non-fatal: the `.php` file is still written, but debugging and stack-trace mapping for that file will not have a `.map` companion.

The build continues. Inspect the detail in the warning for the underlying exception, then retry with `build.generateSourcemap` enabled after fixing the cause.
:::

:::member[TYHP5021 (Warning)]
**EmitterSourceMapWriteFailed.** Message: <code>Failed to write source map file `{0}`: {1}</code>.

The compiler writes a `.php.map` file next to each generated PHP file when `build.generateSourcemap` is true. A write failure (permissions, disk full, invalid path) is non-fatal: the PHP output is still usable without the map.

The build continues. Fix the path or permissions named in the warning and rebuild to produce the missing source map file.
:::

:::member[TYHP5022 (Warning)]
**EmitterSourceMapInvalidMapping.** Message: <code>Invalid source mapping in file `{0}`: generated position (`{1}`,`{2}`) references invalid source position (`{3}`,`{4}`)</code>.

A source mapping segment points at a generated PHP position whose original `.tyhp` line or column is invalid (negative, or otherwise not a real start position). The mapping is skipped; remaining segments are still emitted.

This is non-fatal. If mappings look wrong in a debugger, report the generated and original coordinates from this warning — they identify the emit item whose AST provider had a bad span.
:::

:::member[TYHP5023 (Error)]
**EmitterGenericRuntimeLayoutUnsupported.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\GenericRuntime]` layouts `{0}` have no intersection with this compiler{1}</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP5023</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::


## Configuration Errors (TYHP6xxx)

Configuration errors are reported when `tyhp.json` or CLI options are invalid.

:::member[TYHP6001 (Error)]
**ConfigUnknownError.** Message: <code>Configuration error</code>.

A generic configuration error that does not match a more specific code.
:::

:::member[TYHP6002 (Error)]
**ConfigMissingRequiredField.** Message: <code>Required configuration field is missing</code>.

A required field in `tyhp.json` is not present.
:::

:::member[TYHP6003 (Warning)]
**ConfigInvalidValue.** Message: <code>Invalid configuration value for `{0}`: `{1}`</code>.

A configuration value is out of range, the wrong type, or otherwise invalid.
:::

:::member[TYHP6004 (Error)]
**ConfigInvalidGlobPattern.** Message: <code>Invalid glob pattern in configuration</code>.

An include or exclude glob pattern in `tyhp.json` is malformed.
:::

:::member[TYHP6005 (Error)]
**ConfigOutputPathNotWritable.** Message: <code>Output path is not writable</code>.

The configured output directory does not exist and cannot be created, or the process does not have write permissions.
:::

:::member[TYHP6006 (Warning)]
**ConfigInvalidPhpVersion.** Message: <code>Unsupported PHP version `{0}`; using default `8.4`</code>.

The `output.phpVersion` configuration specifies a PHP version that is not recognized or supported.
:::

:::member[TYHP6007 (Error)]
**ConfigPsr4InvalidMapping.** Message: <code>Invalid PSR-4 mapping in configuration</code>.

A `psr4` configuration entry maps a namespace to a path that is invalid or does not exist.
:::

:::member[TYHP6008 (Warning)]
**ConfigInvalidProjectType.** Message: <code>Unrecognized project type `{0}`; using `application`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP6008</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP6009 (Error)]
**ConfigInterpolationFailed.** Message: <code>Cannot expand `{0}` in `{1}`: {2}</code>.

A placeholder in `tyhp.json` could not be expanded during interpolation. Path keys such as `output.path`, `output.publishPath`, `cache-dir`, `psr4` values, and `output.publishContent` src/dst/exclude support `{name}`-style variables.

`{name}` and `{version}` (and `{projectVersion}`) come from `composer.json` next to `tyhp.json`, not from a file `build.updateComposer` may write under `output.publishPath`. `{version.suffix}` is everything after the numeric patch and is empty when omitted. `{type}` is the tyhp.json project kind. `{composer.type}` is Composer's `type`. `{phpVersion.id}` is the Tyhp PHP id for `output.phpVersion` (`8.2` → `802`). `{env.NAME}` reads a process environment variable; it is an error if that variable is unset.

File variables (`{fileName}`, `{fileStem}`, `{extension}`, `{recursiveDir}`, `{relativePath}`) are only valid in `output.publishContent` `dst`, and expand after glob matching. `{extension}`, `{fileStem}`, and `{recursiveDir}` may be empty. Use `{{` and `}}` for a literal brace. `tyhp init` does not write `version` into `composer.json`; add that field before using `{version}`.
:::

:::member[TYHP6010 (Warning)]
**ConfigStructBackingIgnored.** Message: <code>`build.structBacking` is `{0}`; structs are always PHP arrays, so the setting is ignored. Remove it from tyhp.json</code>.

`tyhp.json` sets `build.structBacking` to a value other than `"array"`. Structs always compile to plain PHP associative arrays, so the build ignores the value. Delete the `build.structBacking` entry (or leave it as `"array"`).
:::

:::member[TYHP7700 (Error)]
**ComposerDisjointExtraRequire.** Message: <code>`extra.tyhp.require` constraint `{0}` for `{1}` is disjoint from existing pin `{2}`</code>.

:::member[TYHP7701 (Error)]
**ComposerStaleExtraRequire.** Message: <code>Stale extra `{0}` is missing from root require-dev or is not installed</code>.

An installed package listed a stale extra.tyhp.require name that is not in this project's root require-dev (and not in require) or is not installed. The compiler cannot type-check against ambient types that are not loaded. Run `tyhp composer sync` or `tyhp build --fix` to write require-dev from the installed extra closure. If extras on packages that are not installed yet are unknown, run `composer update` so the tyhp/core plugin can resolve them. This check is local only and does not fetch Packagist.
:::

:::member[TYHP7702 (Warning)]
**ComposerMissingCompilerPin.** Message: <code>`tyhp/compiler` is missing from root require-dev while `{0}` is in the graph</code>.

`tyhp/compiler` must be pinned on the application root require-dev whenever `tyhp/core` is in the Composer graph. The native CLI can keep running without that pin, so this is a warning unless `--strict` or `build.strictMode` is set. Run `tyhp composer sync` or `tyhp build --fix` to add the compiler pin.
:::

:::member[TYHP7703 (Error)]
**ComposerRootJsonWriteFailed.** Message: <code>root `composer.json` at `{0}` cannot be parsed or written: {1}</code>.

The root composer.json could not be parsed or written while syncing extra.tyhp.require onto require-dev. Fix the JSON (or file permissions) and re-run `tyhp composer sync`.
:::

**IntegrityCheckConfigInvalid.** Message: <code>Integrity check failed: project configuration is invalid</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP7800</code> for the long-form explanation.

Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP7803</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP7900 (Error)]
**OverlayInvalidArguments.** Message: <code>Invalid `tyhp overlay` command `{0}`; expected `create &lt;FQN&gt;` or `stamp` [`&lt;FQN&gt;`]</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP7900</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP7901 (Error)]
**OverlayTargetNotFound.** Message: <code>Overlay target `{0}` was not found</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP7901</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP7902 (Error)]
**OverlayManifestUpdateFailed.** Message: <code>Failed to update overlay glob in `{0}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP7902</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP7903 (Error)]
**OverlayWriteFailed.** Message: <code>Failed to write overlay tyhpdef for `{0}`</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP7903</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP7904 (Error)]
**OverlayCreateOnExtern.** Message: <code>`overlay create` cannot target `extern` type `{0}`</code>.

`tyhp overlay create` copies a real declaration into a hand-written overlay so that declaration can be replaced. An `extern` type is a name-only placeholder with no members; copying it would write a hollow `class { }` that looks like a complete empty type.

Write a full overlay `class` / `interface` / `enum` of the same name to upgrade the placeholder, or `omit` it. Extra `extern` names belong in an include file that regen does not overwrite, not in an overlay created from the placeholder.
:::

:::member[TYHP7905 (Error)]
**OverlayPhpRuntimeUnavailable.** Message: <code>Managed PHP runtime for `{0}` is unavailable</code>.

`tyhp overlay stamp` writes `@overlay-against` once per managed PHP version. Each pass uses that version's managed runtime and stamps only declarations whose `declare(php=…)` or `#[\Tyhp\Php]` gate that runtime satisfies.

This error means the managed runtime for the named version is unavailable, so that pass is skipped. Declarations that belong only to that version are left unchanged. They are not stamped from a different PHP version. Restore the managed runtime cache (the same one `generate_tyhpdef` downloads) and run stamp again.
:::


## Tyhpdef Errors (TYHP8xxx)

Tyhpdef errors are reported when loading or validating type-definition files.

:::member[TYHP8001 (Error)]
**TyhpdefParseError.** Message: <code>Failed to parse tyhpdef file: {0}</code>.

A `.tyhpdef` file contains syntax errors and could not be parsed.

Fix: Check the tyhpdef file for syntax errors. Tyhpdef syntax is similar to Tyhp but only supports declarations (no function bodies).
:::

:::member[TYHP8002 (Error)]
**TyhpdefDuplicateDeclaration.** Message: <code>Tyhpdef declares symbol `{0}` which already exists</code>.

A tyhpdef file declares a symbol (class, function, constant) that is already declared by another tyhpdef or by the project's source code.

The primary span is the later include-layer declaration. A secondary span labeled "declared here" points at the first declaration of that name.

```tyhpdef
<?tyhpdef
class \App\User { }  // first include — labeled "declared here"
```

```tyhpdef
<?tyhpdef
class \App\User { }  // Error: Tyhpdef declares symbol `\App\User` which already exists
```
:::

:::member[TYHP8003 (Error)]
**TyhpdefFileNotFound.** Message: <code>Configured tyhpdef path `{0}` does not exist</code>.

A tyhpdef file path specified in `tyhp.json` or via CLI arguments does not exist on disk.
:::

:::member[TYHP8004 (Error)]
**TyhpdefInvalidFormat.** Message: <code>Tyhpdef file `{0}` has an unexpected structure</code>.

A tyhpdef file was parsed but its structure or format does not match what the compiler expects (e.g., missing required sections, invalid nesting).
:::

:::member[TYHP8005 (Error)]
**TyhpdefBindError.** Message: <code>Tyhpdef bind error: {0}</code>.

A `.tyhpdef` file parsed, but binding it into the symbol table failed. The placeholder is the underlying bind exception text.

This is a semantic bind failure, not a parse error (TYHP8001).

Fix: Check the tyhpdef for unresolved names, illegal members, or other bind-time problems named in the message.
:::

:::member[TYHP8010 (Error)]
**TyhpdefExtensionConflict.** Message: <code>Extension member `{0}` conflicts with a declared member on class `{1}`</code>.

A tyhpdef inline extension declares a member that collides with a member already declared on the same class.
:::

:::member[TYHP8011 (Error)]
**TyhpdefExtensionNotFound.** Message: <code>A `use extension` reference in tyhpdef does not resolve to `{0}`</code>.

A `use extension` reference inside a tyhpdef file points to an extension that does not exist.
:::

:::member[TYHP8012 (Error)]
**TyhpdefInlineExtensionInvalidMember.** Message: <code>Invalid member with the `extension` qualifier in tyhpdef</code>.

A member marked with the `extension` qualifier inside a tyhpdef declaration is not a valid extension member.
:::

:::member[TYHP8013 (Error)]
**TyhpdefExtensionOperatorRequiresBody.** Message: <code>`extension operator {0}` requires a thin `=&gt;` expression; use bodyless `operator {0}(…);` (without `extension`) for native PHP operators</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP8013</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP8014 (Error)]
**TyhpdefPartialTargetNotFound.** Message: <code>`partial` type `{0}` does not exist in this compilation&#39;s include set</code>.
Run <code>tyhp --explain TYHP8014</code> for the long-form explanation.
:::

:::member[TYHP8015 (Error)]
**TyhpdefPropertyHookBodyNotAllowed.** Message: <code>Tyhpdef property hooks must be bodyless</code>.

A tyhpdef hooked property is a bodyless signature list: `{ get; set; }`, `{ get; }`, or `{ &get; set; }`. Brace and arrow bodies (`get { … }`, `get => …`) belong in `.tyhp` source, not `.tyhpdef`.

Write `public string $name { get; set; }` to describe a hooked PHP property. A hooked declaration names one `$name`.
:::

:::member[TYHP8016 (Error)]
**TyhpdefPhpVersionGateOnPropertyHook.** Message: <code>`#[\Tyhp\Php]` is not allowed on a property hook; place it on the property or wrap with `declare(php=...)`</code>.

`#[\Tyhp\Php]` on an individual `get` or `set` is not a version gate. Place the attribute on the property, or wrap the declaration with `declare(php=…)`.

```tyhp
<?tyhpdef
class Holder {
    #[\Tyhp\Php(">=8.4")]
    public string $name { get; set; }
}
```
:::

:::member[TYHP8028 (Error)]
**TyhpdefExternIllegalDeclaration.** Message: <code>`extern` name `{0}` is not name-only</code>.

An `extern` declaration must be name-only: `extern \Foo\Bar;`, `extern class \Foo\Bar;` (or `interface` / `enum`), `extern function \bcadd;`, or `extern const \FOO;` with a semicolon and no members or signature. A body, members, generics, `extends` / `implements` on the placeholder, an `as` alias, `abstract` / `final` / `readonly`, a backing type on `enum`, `extern trait`, or a parameter list / return type / value on `extern function` / `const` is an illegal declaration.

Grammar rejects most of these at parse time. This code is for visitor or binder paths that still see an invalid form.
:::

:::member[TYHP8029 (Error)]
**TyhpdefExternKindMismatch.** Message: <code>Name `{0}` is declared as `{1}` and `{2}`</code>.

The kind of an `extern` placeholder does not match another declaration of the same name in the same PHP name space. `extern class Foo` against a real `interface Foo`, or `extern class Foo` against `extern interface Foo`, is a kind mismatch. A kind-unspecified `extern Foo;` is compatible with a later real class, interface, or enum. Functions, constants, and types occupy separate PHP name spaces, so `extern function Foo` may coexist with `class Foo`.

A later real declaration of the same fully-qualified name and kind silently replaces a compatible placeholder. Two externs of the same kind merge. This diagnostic is only the kind conflict. The `{1}` and `{2}` placeholders are the two kinds (for example `extern class` and `interface`).
:::

:::member[TYHP8030 (Error)]
**TyhpdefPartialOnExtern.** Message: <code>`partial` cannot target `extern` `{0}`</code>.

Overlay or include `partial` targeted an `extern` name. Partial would add members or attributes to a name-only placeholder, which is not allowed.

Full overlay replace with a real `class` / `interface` / `enum` / `function` / `const` of the same name upgrades the placeholder (a kind-unspecified `extern \Name;` accepts class, interface, or enum). `omit` of an extern is allowed and removes the name.
:::

:::member[TYHP8031 (Warning)]
**TyhpdefPartialFunctionTargetNotFound.** Message: <code>Overlay `partial function` has no matching `{0}` in the environment; skipped</code>.

Overlay `partial function` names a function or method that is not in the environment left by include files and earlier overlays. The missing target is skipped; no attributes are merged.

Match the Tyhp name of an existing callable. `partial function` does not add a new symbol. Use a full overlay function or method declaration to introduce a name.
:::

:::member[TYHP8032 (Error)]
**TyhpdefPartialFunctionOutsideOverlay.** Message: <code>`partial function` is only allowed in overlay tyhpdef files</code>.

`partial function` is overlay-only. It merges attributes onto an existing callable without restating the signature.

Using it outside an overlay file is an error. Put name-only `partial function` declarations in an overlay tyhpdef (`extra.tyhp.package` / `tyhp.json` `"overlay"`). Include / baseline files still declare full signatures.
:::

:::member[TYHP8033 (Error)]
**TyhpdefPartialFunctionMemberOutsidePartialType.** Message: <code>`partial function` as a member is only allowed inside overlay `partial` types</code>.

A `partial function` member is only valid inside an overlay `partial` type. That is the merge path that keeps other members and unions attributes onto the matching method.

Write `partial class DateTime { #[\Tyhp\Optimize\Pure] partial function format; }`. A full overlay class replace restates methods with their signatures instead.
:::

:::member[TYHP8034 (Error)]
**TyhpdefPartialTypeHeaderOutsideOverlay.** Message: <code>`partial {0}` header form (semicolon) is only allowed in overlay tyhpdef files</code>.

The semicolon header form `partial class Foo<T>;` (also interface / trait / enum) is overlay-only. It replaces written header clauses on an existing type and keeps unlisted members.

Using it outside an overlay file is an error. Put header-only `partial` declarations in an overlay tyhpdef (`extra.tyhp.package` / `tyhp.json` `"overlay"`). Include / baseline files still use brace `partial` to add members, or a full type declaration.
:::

:::member[TYHP8035 (Warning)]
**TyhpdefPartialTypeHeaderNoEffect.** Message: <code>Overlay `partial {0} {1};` does not change the type</code>.

A bare overlay `partial class Foo;` has no effect: it does not change generics, inheritance, attributes, or names. It is only useful as a keep so the same overlay file can also declare `partial class Foo as Bar;`.

Add generics, `extends` / `implements`, attributes, or `as`, or pair the bare keep with an alias in the same overlay file. Otherwise omit the declaration.
:::
